sec01-card-sec01-F37.front: How does a hearing-impaired applicant arrange an interpreter, and what number reaches the Vermont Relay Service?
sec01-card-sec01-F37.expected_back: A hearing impaired applicant will be provided an interpreter if one is requested when the appointment is scheduled, and the Vermont Relay Service for text telephone users is reached by calling seven one one.

sec01-card-sec01-F38.front: What seven abilities, conditions, and road-sharing attitudes do Vermont driving exams evaluate?
sec01-card-sec01-F38.expected_back: The driving tests check whether you can read road signs and lights, know the state's driving laws, see well enough to drive safely, have safe and courteous driving skills, have any disability affecting safe operation, will maintain your vehicle and will respect bicyclists, motorcyclists, pedestrians and other drivers.

sec01-card-sec01-F39.front: What eyesight standard applies at screening, and what happens if an applicant falls short?
sec01-card-sec01-F39.expected_back: The vision screening checks whether your sight meets the required standard of twenty forty, and an applicant who does not meet it is referred, at their own expense, to a licensed optometrist or ophthalmologist who evaluates whether any restrictions belong on the driving privilege.

sec01-card-sec01-F40.front: Where is the knowledge exam taken, how many four-choice questions appear, and how many pass?
sec01-card-sec01-F40.expected_back: The knowledge test is taken online and has twenty questions, each with four answer choices of which only one is correct, and you must answer at least sixteen questions correctly to pass.

sec01-card-sec01-F41.front: At least how long must you wait before retaking a failed knowledge test?
sec01-card-sec01-F41.expected_back: An applicant who fails the knowledge test must wait at least one day before taking it again.

sec01-card-sec01-F42.front: When may you take the road test, and what real-world practice hours does the handbook expect beforehand?
sec01-card-sec01-F42.memory_hook: Last step, forty hours, five traffic
sec01-card-sec01-F42.expected_back: The road test is given only after every other part of the test has been passed, and the handbook expects at least forty hours of real driving experience beforehand, guided by an experienced driver or instructor, with at least five of those hours in traffic.

sec01-card-sec01-F43.front: What rules govern examiner instructions during the road test, and what passengers or pets are barred?
sec01-card-sec01-F43.memory_hook: Zero tricks, obey rules, no pets
sec01-card-sec01-F43.expected_back: During the road test you will never be asked to do anything against the law and no tricks are played, you must follow the directions of the examiner riding with you, handle the vehicle with skill, drive at proper speeds for conditions and obey signs and rules, and no animals are allowed in the vehicle.

sec01-card-sec01-F44.front: How long is the minimum wait after failing a road test once versus failing a third time?
sec01-card-sec01-F44.expected_back: Failing the road test means waiting at least one week before another try, and after a third failed road test the minimum wait rises to one month.

sec01-card-sec01-R05.front: How do the knowledge-test retake wait and the two road-test retake waits compare?
sec01-card-sec01-R05.expected_back: A failed road test brings a one week wait, but a third failure raises the wait to at least one month, and neither matches the one day wait after a failed knowledge test.

sec01-card-sec01-F23.front: What certificate follows passing a high-school instructor's road test, and what five items unlock the license?
sec01-card-sec01-F23.expected_back: A student who passes a high school instructor's road test gets a Driver Education Examination Certificate, and the license is issued only after that certificate, a valid learner's permit, a parent-signed application, the fees and proof of Vermont residency are handed in at a motor vehicle customer service office.

sec01-card-sec01-F24.front: Which two authorities can pull a provisional junior driver's license away?
sec01-card-sec01-F24.expected_back: A junior driver's license is a provisional license: the Commissioner of Motor Vehicles may take it away when your actions show you are an unsafe driver, and it can also be taken away when your parent or guardian withdraws permission for you to drive.

sec01-card-sec01-F25.front: How long are junior license holders barred from driving on the job, and what paid hauling is never allowed?
sec01-card-sec01-F25.memory_hook: One year or eighteen, never hire
sec01-card-sec01-F25.expected_back: A junior license holder may not drive a vehicle in the course of employment, such as delivering pizza, until the junior license has been held for one year or the holder turns eighteen, whichever comes first, and may never carry passengers for hire.

sec01-card-sec01-F26.front: Who may ride with a junior driver during the first three months, and what cap applies with supervision?
sec01-card-sec01-F26.expected_back: During the first three months on a junior driver's license the holder must drive alone unless a qualified supervisor is in the front seat, the same parent, guardian, instructor or licensed person at least twenty-five years old who may supervise a permit holder, and with one present the only passenger limit is the number of safety belts.

sec01-card-sec01-R04.front: How do unsupervised passenger rules progress across the three stages of a junior license?
sec01-card-sec01-R04.expected_back: The junior license passenger rules move in three steps: driving alone for the first three months, family members during the second three months, and no passenger limit after six months, with the safety belt count capping every step.

sec01-card-sec01-F27.front: How do passenger permissions expand after three months and after six months on a junior license?
sec01-card-sec01-F27.expected_back: During the second three months on a junior driver's license the holder may begin transporting family members, and after six months there is no limit on passengers, but at every stage the driver may never carry more passengers than there are safety belts.

sec01-card-sec01-F28.front: Which actions and handheld gadgets are banned while operating a motor vehicle?
sec01-card-sec01-F28.expected_back: No driver may use any portable electronic device while operating a motor vehicle, which includes reading and manually composing or sending texts, instant messages and emails, and the devices covered include cellular phones, personal digital assistants, tablets and laptop computers.

sec01-card-sec01-F29.front: At what age does a standard driver's license start, and which two noncommercial vehicles still need extra exams?
sec01-card-sec01-F29.expected_back: A driver's license is issued to eligible people aged eighteen or older who pass the required examination, and it allows driving any noncommercial vehicle except a school bus or a motorcycle, each of which needs additional exams.

sec01-card-sec01-F30.front: Who and what vehicle items must accompany a permit holder arriving for a full-license road test?
sec01-card-sec01-F30.expected_back: For the full license road test a permit holder brings a qualified supervisor whose license is valid that day, the same parent, guardian, instructor or licensed person at least twenty-five years old who may supervise a permit holder, plus proof of insurance and registration for a sound, inspected vehicle with a working parking brake.

sec01-card-sec01-F11.front: How long must you hold a learner's permit and keep a violation-free record before getting a junior license?
sec01-card-sec01-F11.expected_back: To get a junior driver's license you must have held a learner's permit for at least one year and kept a clean record with no permit recalls, suspensions or revocations during the six months before applying.

sec01-card-sec01-R02.front: How does the one-year permit holding clock differ from the six-month clean-record clock?
sec01-card-sec01-R02.expected_back: The one year a learner's permit must be held before a junior license is a different clock from the six month clean record period, which counts only the six months immediately before applying.

sec01-card-sec01-F12.front: Which age group qualifies for a junior driver's license, and whose signature authorizes the exam?
sec01-card-sec01-F12.expected_back: A junior driver's license is issued to a sixteen or seventeen year old who passes the required examination, and a parent or legal guardian must sign the application to give permission for the test.

sec01-card-sec01-F13.front: What three hour totals make up an approved teen driver-education course?
sec01-card-sec01-F13.memory_hook: Thirty classroom, six drive, six watch
sec01-card-sec01-F13.expected_back: Before getting a license, every sixteen and seventeen year old must pass a state approved driver education and training course made up of thirty hours of classroom study, six hours of behind the wheel training and six hours of observation.

sec01-card-sec01-F14.front: How many extra practice hours and night hours are required, and what clock window defines nighttime?
sec01-card-sec01-F14.expected_back: On top of the driver education course, a junior license applicant must complete forty hours of driving practice with at least ten hours at night, and nighttime means the period from thirty minutes after sunset to thirty minutes before sunrise.

sec01-card-sec01-F15.front: How does the three-year expiration line affect taking a road test on an expired learner's permit?
sec01-card-sec01-F15.expected_back: An applicant may take the road test on a learner's permit that has been expired for no more than three years and was renewed before the exam, but a permit expired for more than three years requires a written exam before the road test can be given.

sec01-card-sec01-F16.front: What instructor, curriculum, and letterhead proof are needed for out-of-state driver education to count in Vermont?
sec01-card-sec01-F16.expected_back: Driver education taken outside Vermont counts only if a certified or licensed driver education instructor taught it with both classroom and behind the wheel training, and a completion certificate not issued by a state agency needs documentation on state letterhead listing the program's minimum requirements.

sec01-card-sec01-F17.front: Who certifies your forty practice hours, which two tracking tools qualify, and do driver-ed hours count toward them?
sec01-card-sec01-F17.expected_back: A parent or guardian must certify the forty hours of practice driving, at least ten of them at night, using the Driving Practice Log Sheet or the RoadReady app, and the law requires those forty hours to be in addition to the six behind the wheel hours of driver education.

sec01-card-sec01-R03.front: Can the six behind-the-wheel hours from driver education be counted inside your forty certified practice hours?
sec01-card-sec01-R03.expected_back: The forty hours of certified practice driving are counted separately from the six behind the wheel hours of the driver education course, so the two never overlap.

sec01-card-sec01-F03.front: How does Vermont treat holding a license, and how must license holders treat every road user?
sec01-card-sec01-F03.expected_back: Licensing makes driving a privilege rather than a right, so a license holder must drive within the limits of the law and treat every highway user, including bicyclists, motorcyclists and pedestrians, with courtesy and consideration.

sec01-card-sec01-F04.front: Which six types of driving permits, licenses, and privilege cards does Vermont issue?
sec01-card-sec01-F04.memory_hook: Permit, junior, full, commercial, enhanced, card
sec01-card-sec01-F04.expected_back: Vermont issues six kinds of license: the learner's permit, the driver's license, the junior driver's license, the commercial driver's license, the enhanced driver's license and the driver's privilege card.

sec01-card-sec01-F05.front: At what age can a Vermont resident test for a learner's permit, and which out-of-state students also qualify?
sec01-card-sec01-F05.expected_back: A Vermont resident must be at least fifteen years old to take the learner's permit test, and a resident of another state who is enrolled in a Vermont driver education and training course can also get a Vermont learner's permit with a school letter confirming enrollment.

sec01-card-sec01-F06.front: Who signs a minor's permit form, when is no signature needed, and what rule covers foreign exchange students?
sec01-card-sec01-F06.expected_back: A permit applicant who is fifteen, sixteen or seventeen needs a parent or legal guardian to sign the application before taking the test unless the applicant is an emancipated minor, and a foreign exchange student uses a Foreign Exchange Parental Authorization form that a host parent cannot sign.

sec01-card-sec01-F07.front: Which two steps directly trigger issuance of a Vermont learner's permit?
sec01-card-sec01-F07.expected_back: The learner's permit is issued after the applicant passes the online permit test and pays the required fees.

sec01-card-sec01-F08.front: How long must a minor's driving record stay clean before getting a learner's permit?
sec01-card-sec01-F08.expected_back: A learner's permit applicant under eighteen must have kept a clean driving record for the previous two years, and anyone with recalls, suspensions or revocations should contact the DMV because an additional waiting period may be required.

sec01-card-sec01-F09.front: Who qualifies to ride in the front passenger seat while a learner's permit holder drives in Vermont?
sec01-card-sec01-F09.expected_back: With a valid learner's permit you may drive anywhere in Vermont at any time, provided the front seat holds a qualified supervisor: a licensed, unimpaired parent or guardian, an unimpaired licensed or certified driver education instructor, or a licensed, unimpaired person at least twenty-five years old.

sec01-card-sec01-F10.front: What must a Vermont learner's permit holder check before driving in another state?
sec01-card-sec01-F10.expected_back: Before driving in another state on a Vermont learner's permit, check with that state's motor vehicle agency or its law enforcement whether the permit is honored there.

sec01-card-sec01-F01.front: Within how many days of moving to Vermont must a new resident transfer a valid out-of-state driver's license?
sec01-card-sec01-F01.expected_back: A Vermont resident who plans to drive in Vermont must hold a Vermont driver's license, and a new resident arriving with a valid license from another jurisdiction must get a Vermont license within sixty days of moving in.

sec01-card-sec01-R01.front: How does the new-resident transfer deadline differ between a standard license and a commercial license?
sec01-card-sec01-R01.expected_back: The sixty day window to get a Vermont license after moving in applies to a regular license, while a commercial license from another state must be transferred within the shorter window of thirty days.

sec01-card-sec01-F02.front: Within how many days of establishing Vermont residency must a commercial driver's license be transferred?
sec01-card-sec01-F02.expected_back: A person who holds a commercial driver's license from another state must transfer that commercial license to Vermont within thirty days of establishing residency.

sec01-card-sec01-F18.front: What Social Security proof and scheduling step apply when applying for a junior license?
sec01-card-sec01-F18.expected_back: A junior license applicant must put a Social Security number on the application, or supply a Social Security Administration letter showing ineligibility for one, and must book an exam appointment.

sec01-card-sec01-F21.front: What three requirements convert an out-of-state junior license into a Vermont junior license?
sec01-card-sec01-F21.expected_back: An out-of-state junior driver's license converts to a Vermont junior license by passing the required examinations, proving completion of a state approved driver education program and proving an additional forty hours of driving.

sec01-card-sec01-F22.front: When may a high-school driver-education teacher administer the official license road test?
sec01-card-sec01-F22.expected_back: Some DMV licensed high school driver education instructors conduct driver's license road tests, but only at schools that have enrolled in the testing program and only through instructors certified as examiners by the Department of Motor Vehicles.

sec01-card-sec01-F31.front: Which tests must a new resident take if their out-of-state license is current or expired up to three years versus longer?
sec01-card-sec01-F31.expected_back: A new Vermont resident holding a valid out-of-state license, or one expired for three years or less, takes an eye examination to get a Vermont license, while a license expired for more than three years or no license at all means taking the vision, written and road tests.

sec01-card-sec01-R06.front: Why does the three-year expiration mark matter so much for a transferring new resident?
sec01-card-sec01-R06.expected_back: A new resident whose out-of-state license is valid or expired three years or less needs only an eye examination, while one expired more than three years must take the vision, written and road tests like a first-time applicant.

sec01-card-sec01-F32.front: Which three categories of people are refused a Vermont driver's license?
sec01-card-sec01-F32.expected_back: A license is refused to anyone whose driving privilege is suspended, revoked or refused in any state until that action ends and written reinstatement notice arrives, to anyone the Commissioner has evidence cannot or will not drive without endangering others, and to anyone who is not a Vermont resident.

sec01-card-sec01-F49.front: How long must an out-of-state junior license have been held to avoid Vermont's graduated restrictions?
sec01-card-sec01-F49.expected_back: A holder of an out-of-state junior driver's license who applies for a Vermont junior license stays subject to Vermont's graduated license provisions unless the other state's junior license was held for at least six months.

sec01-card-sec01-F19.front: What vehicle condition, brake, and two documents are mandatory at a junior road test?
sec01-card-sec01-F19.expected_back: The vehicle brought to a junior license road test must be clean, in good mechanical condition, legal, carry a valid inspection sticker and have a properly working emergency or parking brake, and failing to show a valid insurance card and registration certificate prevents testing.

sec01-card-sec01-F20.front: Which four specific details must appear on the insurance card presented at a road test?
sec01-card-sec01-F20.expected_back: The insurance card shown at a road test must state the name of the insurance carrier, the effective and expiration dates of coverage, the name of the insured and a description of the vehicle including its vehicle identification number.

sec01-card-sec01-F33.front: At what weight rating or passenger capacity does driving a school bus require a commercial license?
sec01-card-sec01-F33.expected_back: A school bus with a gross vehicle weight rating of twenty-six thousand one pounds or more, or built for sixteen or more passengers including the driver, requires a commercial driver's license with passenger and school bus endorsements.

sec01-card-sec01-R07.front: How does the sixteen-passenger threshold split Type Two endorsements from commercial school-bus licensing?
sec01-card-sec01-R07.memory_hook: Under sixteen Type Two, above commercial
sec01-card-sec01-R07.expected_back: A Type Two school bus endorsement on a regular license covers buses rated for fewer than sixteen passengers, while sixteen or more passengers or a heavy weight rating moves the driver into commercial licensing with passenger and school bus endorsements.

sec01-card-sec01-F34.front: Which non-traditional vehicles carrying schoolchildren also trigger school-bus endorsement rules?
sec01-card-sec01-F34.expected_back: A school bus endorsement is required to transport school children for hire, such as in a taxi, or in a multifunction school activity bus owned or leased by a school, and may also be required when carrying school children in privately or school owned cars and vans.

sec01-card-sec01-F35.front: Who may earn a motorcycle endorsement, and what does finishing the Vermont Basic Rider Course waive?
sec01-card-sec01-F35.expected_back: Any licensed person aged sixteen or older may get a motorcycle endorsement or motorcycle permit by passing a test, and students who complete the Basic Rider Course of the Vermont Rider Education Program are exempt from the state written and skill exams for the endorsement.

sec01-card-sec01-F36.front: How must all motor-vehicle office visits be arranged, and what if your plans change?
sec01-card-sec01-F36.expected_back: All DMV visits are by appointment only, scheduled through the DMV website, and an applicant who cannot keep an appointment should cancel or reschedule as soon as possible so the time can go to someone else.

sec01-card-sec01-F45.front: When are out-of-state cars, rental cars, or dealer-plated vehicles accepted for a road test?
sec01-card-sec01-F45.memory_hook: Any state legal, rental letter, family
sec01-card-sec01-F45.expected_back: You must furnish a registered, inspected and insured vehicle for the road test from any state, a rental vehicle is accepted only when the rental company provides a letter accepting full responsibility, and a vehicle on dealer registration is accepted only for an immediate family member of the dealership.

sec01-card-sec01-F46.front: Which three specialty registration plates bar a vehicle from being used in a road test?
sec01-card-sec01-F46.expected_back: No road test is given in a vehicle displaying agriculture, antique or exhibit plates, because the law restricts how those plates may be used.

sec01-card-sec01-F47.front: Along with core lights, glass, tires, and brakes, which two vintage model-year cutoffs govern signals, belts, and defrosters?
sec01-card-sec01-F47.expected_back: A road test vehicle needs working headlights, horn, wipers, rearview mirror, tail lights, tires, steering, windshield, exhaust, brakes, fenders and bumpers, plus directional signals on vehicles made after the start of nineteen fifty-five and safety belts and defrosters on models from nineteen sixty-four on.

sec01-card-sec01-F48.front: How strong must a test vehicle's parking brake be, and what window rule applies up front?
sec01-card-sec01-F48.expected_back: The emergency or parking brake of a road test vehicle must be able to hold it in neutral on any grade where it is operated, both headed uphill and downhill, and illegal tinting of the front windows is not allowed.

sec01-card-sec01-F50.front: Which endorsement on a regular license covers hauling schoolchildren in a bus rated under sixteen passengers?
sec01-card-sec01-F50.expected_back: Carrying school children in a school bus the manufacturer rates for fewer than sixteen passengers requires a Type Two school bus endorsement on the regular driver's license.

sec01-card-sec01-F51.front: Will an examiner ever administer a road test inside a vehicle that lacks safety belts?
sec01-card-sec01-F51.expected_back: No road test is given in a vehicle that does not have safety belts.

sec02-card-sec02-F10.front: Who may ride with a junior driver during the first three months on the license?
sec02-card-sec02-F10.expected_back: During the first three months of driving on a junior driver's license the holder is restricted to driving alone, and passengers are allowed only when a licensed, unimpaired parent or guardian, a licensed or certified unimpaired driver education instructor, or a licensed, unimpaired person at least twenty-five rides in the front seat.

sec02-card-sec02-F11.front: When a qualified supervisor rides up front with a junior driver, what is the only limit on passengers?
sec02-card-sec02-F11.expected_back: When one of the qualified supervising adults is in the vehicle with a junior driver, there is no restriction on how many passengers ride along, except that the driver may never carry more passengers than there are safety belts.

sec02-card-sec02-F12.front: Exactly which family members may ride unsupervised during the second three months of a junior license?
sec02-card-sec02-F12.expected_back: During the second three months on a junior driver's license the holder may begin carrying immediate family members, which the law limits to siblings and parents only.

sec02-card-sec02-R02.front: Do cousins, grandparents, or friends qualify as unsupervised passengers during months four through six?
sec02-card-sec02-R02.memory_hook: Wait six months for cousins, friends
sec02-card-sec02-R02.expected_back: In the second three months of a junior license the only unsupervised passengers allowed are siblings and parents, so cousins, grandparents and friends must wait until the six month mark.

sec02-card-sec02-F13.front: What passenger rule applies once you have held a junior driver's license for six months?
sec02-card-sec02-F13.expected_back: After holding a junior driver's license for six months there is no restriction on the number of passengers, but the driver still may not carry more passengers than there are safety belts.

sec02-card-sec02-F16.front: How long is a junior operator's license recalled for driving on the job or carrying paying passengers?
sec02-card-sec02-F16.expected_back: A learner's permit or junior driver's license is a recallable provisional license, and a junior operator caught carrying passengers for hire or driving for an employer receives a ninety day recall.

sec02-card-sec02-R03.front: How do recall lengths split between hire or job driving versus texting or diversion-board referrals?
sec02-card-sec02-R03.expected_back: Carrying passengers for hire and driving for an employer each cost a junior operator a ninety day recall, while a diversion board recommendation or a texting violation costs thirty days.

sec02-card-sec02-F17.front: What recall terms follow a diversion-board referral versus hitting three speeding points or six total points?
sec02-card-sec02-F17.expected_back: A recall of thirty days follows a recommendation from a diversion or reparative board, while junior operator point accumulation, meaning a single three point speeding violation or a six point total, brings a ninety day recall.

sec02-card-sec02-R04.front: Does a junior operator have to reach six total points before a speeding ticket triggers a recall?
sec02-card-sec02-R04.expected_back: A single speeding violation worth three points triggers the junior operator points recall by itself, the same ninety day recall that a six point total brings.

sec02-card-sec02-F18.front: What recall length, minimum fine, and minimum point hit punish a texting junior operator?
sec02-card-sec02-F18.memory_hook: Thirty days, hundred dollars, two points
sec02-card-sec02-F18.expected_back: Texting as a junior operator brings a thirty day recall, along with fines of at least one hundred dollars and at least two points on the driving record.

sec02-card-sec02-F19.front: What happens to license eligibility during a recall, and what procedural right does the driver hold?
sec02-card-sec02-F19.expected_back: While a recall is in effect the person is ineligible for a junior driver's license or a driver's license, and a person whose permit or license is recalled has the right to a hearing.

sec02-card-sec02-F20.front: How does a recalled permit or junior license return after its term ends, and what fee applies?
sec02-card-sec02-F20.expected_back: A recalled learner's permit or junior driver's license is restored when its specific term expires and, if required, after the holder passes a re-examination, and no reinstatement fee is due for restoring it.

sec02-card-sec02-F03.front: Over what prior timeframe must a learner's permit applicant show a clean driving record?
sec02-card-sec02-F03.expected_back: An applicant for a learner's permit must have kept a clean driving record during the previous two years.

sec02-card-sec02-R01.front: Which clean-record window applies before getting a permit versus before getting a junior license?
sec02-card-sec02-R01.memory_hook: Two years permit, six months junior
sec02-card-sec02-R01.expected_back: The two year clean record requirement applies to getting the learner's permit, while the six month clean record requirement applies to getting the junior driver's license.

sec02-card-sec02-F04.front: At least how long must you hold a learner's permit before upgrading to a junior license?
sec02-card-sec02-F04.expected_back: A learner's permit must be held for at least one year before a junior driver's license can be obtained.

sec02-card-sec02-F05.front: How many total and nighttime practice hours must a qualified supervisor ride beside you for and certify?
sec02-card-sec02-F05.expected_back: Before getting a junior driver's license the permit holder must complete an additional forty hours of practice behind the wheel, at least ten of them nighttime driving, with a qualified supervisor riding beside the driver who then certifies the practice.

sec02-card-sec02-F06.front: How do the forty practice hours relate to driver-ed driving, and what exact clock span counts as night?
sec02-card-sec02-F06.expected_back: The forty practice hours come on top of the six hours of behind the wheel instruction in a driver training course, and nighttime driving for this purpose means the period from thirty minutes after sunset to thirty minutes before sunrise.

sec02-card-sec02-F07.front: What record standard must hold during the six months leading up to a junior driver's license?
sec02-card-sec02-F07.expected_back: A junior driver's license requires a clean record with no learner's permit recalls, suspensions or revocations during the six months before it is obtained.

sec02-card-sec02-F08.front: Until which milestone comes first is a junior driver barred from driving as part of a job?
sec02-card-sec02-F08.expected_back: For one year after a junior driver's license is issued the holder may not drive a vehicle as part of a job, such as delivering pizza, until that year passes or the holder reaches eighteen, whichever comes first.

sec02-card-sec02-F09.front: Is a junior driver's license holder ever allowed to transport passengers for hire?
sec02-card-sec02-F09.expected_back: A junior driver's license holder may not carry passengers for hire.

sec02-card-sec02-F14.front: What six-month record rule governs upgrading a Vermont junior license to a full license at eighteen?
sec02-card-sec02-F14.expected_back: A Vermont junior driver's license holder becomes eligible for a full driver's license at eighteen only with no recalls, suspensions or revocations during the previous six months, and that six month period starts on the date of reinstatement.

sec02-card-sec02-R05.front: After a recall occurs, on which exact date does the six-month clean countdown to a full license restart?
sec02-card-sec02-R05.expected_back: The six clean months needed before a junior driver steps up to a full license are counted from the reinstatement date when a recall happened, not from the day the recall began.

sec02-card-sec02-F15.front: What course, three exams, and six-month rule govern converting another state's junior license to Vermont?
sec02-card-sec02-F15.expected_back: A person with a junior driver's license from another state who applies for a Vermont junior license must prove completion of a state approved driver education course that meets or exceeds Vermont requirements, must pass an eye, written and road test, and stays under the graduated license law unless the other state's license was held for at least six months.

sec02-card-sec02-F01.front: Exactly who falls under Vermont's graduated driver's license law?
sec02-card-sec02-F01.expected_back: Everyone who obtains a learner's permit or a junior driver's license in Vermont is subject to the graduated driver's license law.

sec02-card-sec02-F02.front: Under graduated law, which three categories of unimpaired adults may supervise a fifteen-plus permit driver?
sec02-card-sec02-F02.expected_back: Under the graduated license law a person fifteen or older may operate a vehicle on a valid learner's permit only when a qualified person rides beside the driver: a licensed, unimpaired parent or guardian, a licensed or certified and unimpaired driver education instructor, or a licensed, unimpaired person at least twenty-five years old.

sec02-card-sec02-F21.front: What ranks as the leading cause of teen death and injury, and who plays a critical safety role?
sec02-card-sec02-F21.expected_back: Motor vehicle crashes are the leading cause of death and injury for teenagers, and a parent or guardian has a critical role in shaping a teen's safe driving habits.

sec02-card-sec02-F22.front: Which four risk factors justify staged learning from fifteen to eighteen, and what is the program's goal?
sec02-card-sec02-F22.expected_back: The law requires teens from fifteen to eighteen to learn to drive in stages because young drivers are placed at risk by age, lack of driving experience, passengers and other distractions, and the graduated program exists to save teen lives and reduce injuries even though it cannot prevent every teen crash.

sec02-card-sec02-F23.front: How does the handbook compare national teen deaths from texting behind the wheel against drinking and driving?
sec02-card-sec02-F23.expected_back: The handbook states that more teens in the United States are killed texting while driving than drinking while driving.

sec04-card-sec04-F05.front: Which seven roadway, double-parked, pedestrian, work-zone, bridge, and tunnel spots ban parking?
sec04-card-sec04-F05.expected_back: You may not park on the part of the highway that traffic uses, next to a car already stopped or parked at the street side, on a sidewalk, inside an intersection, on a crosswalk, beside road work where you would block traffic, or on a bridge or in a tunnel.

sec04-card-sec04-F06.front: How far must parked cars stay from railroad rails and fire hydrants, and what driveway rule applies?
sec04-card-sec04-F06.memory_hook: Fifty rail, six hydrant, clear drives
sec04-card-sec04-F06.expected_back: You may not park on railroad tracks, closer than fifty feet to the nearest rail at a crossing, across the mouth of any driveway, or closer than six feet to a fire hydrant.

sec04-card-sec04-R01.front: From shortest to longest, how do Vermont's hydrant, crosswalk, signal, and rail parking clearances step up?
sec04-card-sec04-R01.expected_back: A hydrant needs a six foot clearance, a crosswalk at an intersection twenty feet, a stop sign or signal thirty feet, and a railroad rail fifty feet.

sec04-card-sec04-F07.front: Within how many feet of an intersection crosswalk versus a stop sign or traffic light is parking banned?
sec04-card-sec04-F07.expected_back: Parking is prohibited within twenty feet of a crosswalk at an intersection and within thirty feet of a flashing red or yellow light, a stop sign or a traffic light.

sec04-card-sec04-F08.front: Where signs are posted, how far from a fire-station driveway is parking banned on each side?
sec04-card-sec04-F08.expected_back: Where signs are posted, parking is prohibited within twenty feet of a fire station driveway and, across the street, within seventy-five feet of that driveway.

sec04-card-sec04-R02.front: Which street side carries the twenty-foot versus seventy-five-foot firehouse rule, and when do both apply?
sec04-card-sec04-R02.expected_back: The twenty foot fire station rule applies on the same side of the street, while the seventy-five foot rule applies across the street, and both apply only where signs are posted.

sec04-card-sec04-F09.front: Which three signed or painted zones also forbid general parking?
sec04-card-sec04-F09.expected_back: Parking is also prohibited anywhere an official sign says no parking, on a marked bicycle lane and in a marked disabled parking area.

sec04-card-sec04-F12.front: Whom must you yield to at a roundabout, and what signal is required before leaving?
sec04-card-sec04-F12.expected_back: Drivers must yield to traffic already in the roundabout, enter only when there is a safe gap, yield to pedestrians and bicyclists when entering or exiting, and always signal the intention to exit.

sec04-card-sec04-F13.front: When do you pick your lane for a multilane roundabout, and may you switch lanes once inside?
sec04-card-sec04-F13.expected_back: A multilane roundabout requires reading the lane assignment signs and pavement markings before entering to pick the proper lane, drivers may not change lanes once inside, and mirror and blind spot checks are required before exiting from the inside lane.

sec04-card-sec04-F14.front: In a two-lane roundabout without lane signs or arrows, which turns belong to the right and left lanes?
sec04-card-sec04-F14.expected_back: Entering a two lane roundabout that has no signs or arrows, the right lane may turn right or go through, while the left lane may turn left or go through.

sec04-card-sec04-R05.front: Why must you settle into right-or-through versus left-or-through before crossing a two-lane roundabout line?
sec04-card-sec04-R05.expected_back: In an unmarked two lane roundabout the right lane is for right turns or through travel and the left lane for left turns or through travel, and once inside no lane change is permitted.

sec04-card-sec04-F15.front: How do you yield to an emergency vehicle before entering a roundabout versus once already inside?
sec04-card-sec04-F15.memory_hook: Pull over outside, exit first inside
sec04-card-sec04-F15.expected_back: Always yield to emergency vehicles at a roundabout: if you have not yet entered, pull over and let them pass, and if you are already inside, pull over only after you have safely exited.

sec04-card-sec04-R04.front: What separates a driver's emergency-vehicle duty on a roundabout approach from inside the circle?
sec04-card-sec04-R04.expected_back: An emergency vehicle approaching a roundabout means pulling over before entering, but a driver already circulating keeps going and pulls over only after exiting.

sec04-card-sec04-F02.front: How close to the curb or edge must parked wheels sit, and which direction must the car face?
sec04-card-sec04-F02.expected_back: On a two lane road a parked vehicle's right wheels must sit no more than twelve inches from the curb or road edge, on a one way road the vehicle must be within twelve inches of the roadside, and in both cases it must point the same way as traffic.

sec04-card-sec04-R03.front: How does the twelve-inch curb measurement contrast with the hundred-fifty-foot rural highway rule?
sec04-card-sec04-R03.expected_back: Twelve inches is the curb distance for a parked vehicle, while one hundred fifty feet is the sight distance needed in each direction before parking on a rural highway.

sec04-card-sec04-F03.front: Where must all four wheels rest when parking along a rural highway, and what sightline is required?
sec04-card-sec04-F03.expected_back: When parking on a rural highway all wheels must be off the traveled portion of the road, and you must not stop on a hill, on a curve, anywhere the vehicle cannot be seen for at least one hundred fifty feet in either direction, or in an area posted for no parking.

sec04-card-sec04-F04.front: What two steps prevent a parked vehicle from rolling into traffic on a hill?
sec04-card-sec04-F04.expected_back: When parking on a hill you must make sure the vehicle cannot roll into traffic, so always turn the front wheels and set the parking brake.

sec04-card-sec04-F01.front: Alongside parallel, angle, and perpendicular parking options, what centerline maneuver is never allowed?
sec04-card-sec04-F01.expected_back: Parking options on the road include parallel parking, angle parking to the left or right, and perpendicular parking to the left or right either forward or backward, and a driver must never cross the center line to park.

sec04-card-sec04-F10.front: Which way do vehicles turn and circulate in a roundabout, and what four community benefits result?
sec04-card-sec04-F10.expected_back: A roundabout is an intersection control where traffic enters and exits only by right turns and circulates counterclockwise, and roundabouts reduce vehicle delay, crashes, fuel use and air pollution.

sec04-card-sec04-F11.front: How do roundabouts compare in safety with stop signs or signals, and how fast should you drive them?
sec04-card-sec04-F11.expected_back: In most situations a roundabout moves cars, walkers and cyclists through an intersection more safely than a stop sign or a traffic signal does, and a driver should keep speed low when approaching, circulating and exiting.

sec05-card-sec05-F09.front: How must you treat a completely dark traffic signal versus an out-of-order signal flashing red or yellow?
sec05-card-sec05-F09.memory_hook: Dark means all-way stop, obey flash
sec05-card-sec05-F09.expected_back: Traffic signals control the right-of-way for smooth, orderly traffic flow, a dark signal such as one in a power failure is treated as a stop sign in every direction, and a signal that is out of order and flashing yellow or red must be obeyed as a flashing signal.

sec05-card-sec05-R05.front: Why does a blacked-out signal require something different from a malfunctioning flashing yellow signal?
sec05-card-sec05-R05.memory_hook: Dark stops everyone, flash follows color
sec05-card-sec05-R05.expected_back: A dark traffic signal is treated as a stop sign for every direction, while a signal flashing red or yellow is obeyed as that flashing color.

sec05-card-sec05-F10.front: Where must you halt at a steady red light, and when may you still move while red shows?
sec05-card-sec05-F10.expected_back: At a red light stop before the stop line or the crosswalk, whichever comes first, and wait for green, although a green arrow that comes on during the red allows travel in the arrow's direction.

sec05-card-sec05-F11.front: What three steps precede a legal right turn on circular red, and what blocks it?
sec05-card-sec05-F11.memory_hook: Full stop, scan, yield, check signs
sec05-card-sec05-F11.expected_back: A right turn at a circular red light is usually allowed only after a complete stop, a scan of the intersection and yielding to pedestrians and other vehicles, and some intersections post signs or symbols forbidding a right turn on red.

sec05-card-sec05-F13.front: What does a steady yellow signal warn, and what if you are already too close to stop safely?
sec05-card-sec05-F13.memory_hook: Red coming, clear cautiously if close
sec05-card-sec05-F13.expected_back: A yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red, and a driver who is too close to the intersection to stop safely should proceed through with caution.

sec05-card-sec05-F14.front: What yielding rule still binds a left-turning driver facing a circular green light?
sec05-card-sec05-F14.expected_back: A green light allows you to proceed when it is safe, but a driver turning left must still yield to oncoming vehicles, and where extra emphasis is needed a left turn yield on green sign hangs from the overhead wire near the signal.

sec05-card-sec05-F15.front: Which everyday intersection sign matches the exact rule of a flashing circular red light?
sec05-card-sec05-F15.expected_back: A flashing circular red light is treated exactly like a stop sign: come to a stop, give way to every pedestrian, bicyclist and vehicle, and then go.

sec05-card-sec05-R01.front: How does your pedal requirement differ between a flashing red signal and a flashing yellow signal?
sec05-card-sec05-R01.expected_back: A flashing circular red light requires a full stop like a stop sign, while a flashing yellow light requires only slowing, scanning and yielding before proceeding.

sec05-card-sec05-F16.front: What four actions belong when approaching an intersection with a flashing yellow signal?
sec05-card-sec05-F16.expected_back: A flashing yellow light means slow down, scan the intersection, yield to any oncoming vehicles before attempting a left turn, and proceed with caution.

sec05-card-sec05-F17.front: May a left-turning driver pull into the intersection or turn while a solid red arrow is lit?
sec05-card-sec05-F17.expected_back: A solid red arrow means drivers intending to turn left must stop and wait, and must not enter the intersection to turn while it is displayed.

sec05-card-sec05-F18.front: What does a solid yellow left arrow warn, and who may finish turning on it?
sec05-card-sec05-F18.expected_back: A solid yellow arrow means the left turn signal is about to change to red, so drivers should prepare to stop, or prepare to complete the left turn if they are already legally within the intersection and no conflicting traffic is present.

sec05-card-sec05-F19.front: Why must you yield before turning left on a flashing yellow arrow?
sec05-card-sec05-F19.expected_back: A flashing yellow arrow lets drivers turn left only after yielding to all oncoming traffic, which has a green light, and to any pedestrians in the crosswalk, waiting for a safe gap before turning.

sec05-card-sec05-F20.front: Why does a solid green arrow give left-turning traffic protected right-of-way?
sec05-card-sec05-F20.expected_back: A solid green arrow gives left turns the right-of-way because the oncoming traffic is facing a red light.

sec05-card-sec05-R02.front: What oncoming-signal difference separates a solid green arrow from a flashing yellow arrow?
sec05-card-sec05-R02.memory_hook: Green holds red, flashing faces green
sec05-card-sec05-R02.expected_back: A solid green arrow protects the left turn because oncoming traffic has red, whereas a flashing yellow arrow permits the turn only after yielding to oncoming traffic that has green.

sec05-card-sec05-F05.front: What must you do when a vehicle flashing blue or red lights or sounding a siren approaches from any direction?
sec05-card-sec05-F05.expected_back: When a vehicle with flashing blue or red lights or a sounding siren approaches from any direction, the law requires you to pull over to the right side of the road, stop, and stay stopped until the emergency or law enforcement vehicle has passed.

sec05-card-sec05-R04.front: How does your legal duty differ between an approaching emergency vehicle and one stopped ahead?
sec05-card-sec05-R04.memory_hook: Approaching stops right, stopped moves over
sec05-card-sec05-R04.expected_back: An approaching emergency vehicle requires you to pull right and stop until it passes, while a stopped one requires caution, slowing and where possible a lane change rather than a stop.

sec05-card-sec05-F06.front: How must you pass a stopped police or emergency vehicle flashing blue or red lights, especially on four-lane highways?
sec05-card-sec05-F06.expected_back: When you come upon a stopped police car showing flashing blue lights or a stopped emergency vehicle showing flashing red lights you must slow down and proceed with caution, and on a four lane road like an interstate you must also move over a lane whenever that can be done safely.

sec05-card-sec05-R03.front: Where does Vermont's move-over rule add a lane-change duty on top of slowing down?
sec05-card-sec05-R03.expected_back: A stopped emergency vehicle calls for slowing down everywhere, but the additional duty to change lanes applies only on a four lane highway and only when the change is safe.

sec05-card-sec05-F07.front: Who holds the right-of-way when a state, city, or town maintenance vehicle like a flashing snowplow works the road?
sec05-card-sec05-F07.expected_back: A maintenance vehicle of the state, a city or a town that is working on a highway has the right-of-way, so a driver coming up on a snowplow with its lights flashing must slow with caution and give way to it.

sec05-card-sec05-F08.front: What light color marks towing and repair trucks, and how must you pass them when stopped?
sec05-card-sec05-F08.expected_back: Towing and repair vehicles usually show amber flashing lights, and a driver must use the same caution and procedures around these stopped vehicles as around stopped police and emergency vehicles.

sec05-card-sec05-F01.front: How do police signal a traffic stop, and which two stopping spots must you avoid?
sec05-card-sec05-F01.memory_hook: Pull far right, skip intersections, medians
sec05-card-sec05-F01.expected_back: Police vehicles signal a driver to stop by turning on flashing lights, or flashing lights together with a siren, and the driver should move as close as safely possible to the right side of the road without stopping in an intersection or pulling into the center median of a divided highway.

sec05-card-sec05-F02.front: Why should you leave your safety belt buckled and keep movements minimal as an officer walks up?
sec05-card-sec05-F02.memory_hook: Let officer see belt, stay still
sec05-card-sec05-F02.expected_back: During a police stop keep your safety belt fastened until the officer has seen you wearing it, limit your own movements and those of passengers, breathe deeply and stay calm while the officer explains the reason for the stop.

sec05-card-sec05-F03.front: Which three documents do you show on request, where do you stay, and what light helps in dim areas?
sec05-card-sec05-F03.memory_hook: Three papers, stay inside, dome light
sec05-card-sec05-F03.expected_back: When the officer asks, show your license, vehicle registration and proof of insurance, stay in the vehicle unless asked to get out, and in a dimly lit area turn on the interior lights after stopping and before the officer approaches.

sec05-card-sec05-F04.front: Where is the proper forum to contest or argue a traffic ticket?
sec05-card-sec05-F04.memory_hook: Contest tickets in court, never roadside
sec05-card-sec05-F04.expected_back: The roadside is not the place to argue a traffic offense; the time to address it is in court.

sec05-card-sec05-F12.front: What should you do when a uniformed police officer waves you through a steady red signal?
sec05-card-sec05-F12.expected_back: A police officer may direct you through a red light, and you should follow the officer's directions with caution.

sec05-card-sec05-F21.front: How can you still tell whether a snow- or mud-covered sign regulates, warns, or informs?
sec05-card-sec05-F21.expected_back: A road sign's meaning can be told from its shape and color as well as its wording, so a sign covered by dirt or snow can still be read as regulatory, warning or information from its shape alone.

sec05-card-sec05-F22.front: How many sides does a stop sign have, and behind which of three points must you halt first?
sec05-card-sec05-F22.memory_hook: Eight sides, stop before first line
sec05-card-sec05-F22.expected_back: A stop sign has eight sides; at it you come to a full stop ahead of the stop line, the marked or unmarked crosswalk or the cross road, whichever is reached first, then scan the intersection, give way as required and proceed.

sec05-card-sec05-F23.front: Which sign uses an inverted triangle shape, and what three actions does it require?
sec05-card-sec05-F23.expected_back: A yield right-of-way sign is shaped like an upside down triangle and means slow down, search, and enter only when the way is clear of pedestrians, bicyclists and vehicles.

sec05-card-sec05-F24.front: What hazard ahead is announced by a circular sign marked with a large cross and railroad initials?
sec05-card-sec05-F24.expected_back: A circular sign bearing a large X and the letters RR warns that a railroad crossing is ahead.

sec12-card-sec12-F12.front: What does Vermont law say about reading or sending electronic messages while driving?
sec12-card-sec12-F12.expected_back: It is against the law for a driver to read or send messages while driving.

sec12-card-sec12-F13.front: Where does Vermont's portable electronic device ban apply, including when traffic halts?
sec12-card-sec12-F13.expected_back: Vermont law forbids a driver from using a portable electronic device while operating a vehicle on a public highway, and the ban still applies when the vehicle is stopped.

sec12-card-sec12-R03.front: May you legally check a handheld phone while stopped at a red traffic light in Vermont?
sec12-card-sec12-R03.expected_back: The device ban applies even while the vehicle is stopped on a public highway, so waiting at a red light is not an exception.

sec12-card-sec12-F14.front: What fine ranges apply to a first versus a second-or-later portable electronic device violation?
sec12-card-sec12-F14.expected_back: A first violation of the portable electronic device law carries a fine of at least one hundred dollars and at most two hundred dollars, and a second or later violation a fine of at least two hundred fifty dollars and at most five hundred dollars.

sec12-card-sec12-R01.front: How much higher does Vermont's handheld-device fine jump from offense one to a repeat offense?
sec12-card-sec12-R01.expected_back: A first handheld device violation costs one hundred to two hundred dollars, while a repeat violation costs two hundred fifty to five hundred dollars.

sec12-card-sec12-F15.front: How many points attach to a handheld-device conviction inside an active work zone with crews present?
sec12-card-sec12-F15.expected_back: A conviction for using a portable electronic device while driving in a properly designated work zone with construction, maintenance or utility personnel present adds two points to the driving record for a first conviction and five points for a second or later conviction.

sec12-card-sec12-R02.front: Where do Vermont's handheld-device fines apply compared with its two- and five-point penalties?
sec12-card-sec12-R02.expected_back: Points for handheld device use attach only to convictions inside a designated work zone with workers present, two for a first and five for a repeat, while the fines apply everywhere.

sec12-card-sec12-F16.front: What two safe alternatives exist when an urgent phone call cannot wait during a trip?
sec12-card-sec12-F16.expected_back: Driving requires full attention, so if a call must be made ask a passenger to place it or stop at a safe place first.

sec12-card-sec12-F01.front: What common reaction flaw do studies find across all distracted drivers?
sec12-card-sec12-F01.expected_back: Studies show that anything that takes attention away from driving can result in a crash, and distracted drivers all show the same basic behavior of reacting more slowly to events such as a vehicle stopping to turn left or pulling out from a side road.

sec12-card-sec12-F02.front: How does distraction affect spotting vulnerable road users and judging turn gaps?
sec12-card-sec12-F02.expected_back: Distracted drivers more often fail to notice hazards such as pedestrians, bicyclists or debris, and they shrink their margin of safety, taking risks like turning left in front of oncoming traffic.

sec12-card-sec12-F03.front: Which two driver errors most frequently contribute to pedestrian and bicycle crashes in Vermont?
sec12-card-sec12-F03.expected_back: Inattention and failure to yield are the most common driver actions contributing to pedestrian and bicycle crashes in Vermont.

sec12-card-sec12-F04.front: How should you set radio presets and volume before driving?
sec12-card-sec12-F04.expected_back: Pre program your favorite radio stations and keep the stereo low enough to hear sounds outside the vehicle such as a siren, a horn or a train whistle.

sec12-card-sec12-F05.front: How should you manage navigation with a passenger aboard versus driving solo?
sec12-card-sec12-F05.expected_back: Let a front seat passenger act as co pilot instead of fumbling with maps or navigation, and when driving alone map the destination in advance.

sec12-card-sec12-F06.front: What three precautions apply to food and beverages inside your vehicle?
sec12-card-sec12-F06.expected_back: Avoid eating and drinking while driving, keep food items secure and make sure drinks fit firmly in cup holders.

sec12-card-sec12-F07.front: How should drivers prepare for the distraction potential of young passengers?
sec12-card-sec12-F07.expected_back: Do not underestimate how distracting children can be in the vehicle, and teach them the importance of good behavior while riding.

sec12-card-sec12-F08.front: What should you do if you catch yourself lost in thought or staring at roadside scenes?
sec12-card-sec12-F08.expected_back: Take a break if you find yourself lost in thought while driving, and focus on driving rather than people or objects inside or outside the vehicle.

sec12-card-sec12-F09.front: What rules does the Vermont manual give on grooming, traveling pets, and smoking?
sec12-card-sec12-F09.expected_back: Do personal grooming at home rather than in the vehicle, keep pets in a carrier rather than in your lap or loose, and avoid smoking while driving because it is a distraction.

sec12-card-sec12-F10.front: Which five emotional states hurt safe driving, and how should you handle them first?
sec12-card-sec12-F10.expected_back: Emotions affect safe driving, and you may not drive well when overly worried, excited, afraid, angry or depressed, so give yourself time to cool off and calm down, for example by taking a walk.

sec12-card-sec12-R04.front: How does the cure for intense emotion differ from the cure for time pressure?
sec12-card-sec12-R04.expected_back: Strong emotion is handled by cooling off before driving, while running late is handled by leaving early, two different cures for two different risks.

sec12-card-sec12-F11.front: Why does leaving just a few minutes early make every trip safer?
sec12-card-sec12-F11.expected_back: Plan ahead and leave a few minutes early, because a driver with plenty of time is less likely to speed, break laws or crash.

sec13-card-sec13-F02.front: How many points attach to a Vermont speeding conviction, and what sets the exact amount?
sec13-card-sec13-F02.expected_back: Speeding carries two to eight points depending on how far over the limit you were driving.

sec13-card-sec13-R02.front: Which two Vermont violations carry sliding point ranges rather than fixed point totals?
sec13-card-sec13-R02.expected_back: Speeding and texting both carry point ranges, two to eight for speeding by how far over the limit and two to five for texting, unlike the fixed values of the other listed offenses.

sec13-card-sec13-F03.front: What point range applies to a texting-while-driving conviction in Vermont?
sec13-card-sec13-F03.expected_back: Texting while driving carries two to five points.

sec13-card-sec13-F04.front: How many points attach to driving unlicensed or running a stop sign or red signal?
sec13-card-sec13-F04.expected_back: Driving without a license carries two points, and failing to stop for a stop sign or red light also carries two points.

sec13-card-sec13-R04.front: How do Vermont's points compare between running a red traffic signal and disobeying a police officer?
sec13-card-sec13-R04.expected_back: Running a red light costs two points, but failing to obey a police officer costs four.

sec13-card-sec13-F05.front: How many points attach to disobeying an officer or failing to yield to a crosswalk pedestrian?
sec13-card-sec13-F05.expected_back: Failing to obey a police officer carries four points, and failing to yield the right-of-way to a pedestrian in a crosswalk also carries four points.

sec13-card-sec13-R01.front: How do failure-to-yield points differ between a crosswalk pedestrian and an emergency responder?
sec13-card-sec13-R01.expected_back: Failing to yield to a pedestrian in a crosswalk is four points, while failing to yield to an ambulance, fire truck or police officer is five points.

sec13-card-sec13-F06.front: How many points attach to failing to yield for an ambulance, fire truck, or police officer?
sec13-card-sec13-F06.expected_back: Failing to yield the right-of-way to an ambulance, fire truck or police officer carries five points.

sec13-card-sec13-F07.front: How many points attach to passing a stopped school bus displaying flashing red warning lights?
sec13-card-sec13-F07.expected_back: Failing to stop for a school bus stopped with its red warning lights flashing carries five points.

sec13-card-sec13-F08.front: What notice goes out at ten accumulated points, and what review may the driver request?
sec13-card-sec13-F08.expected_back: When a driver accumulates ten points a letter is sent announcing that the driving privilege will be suspended, and the driver may request a hearing to verify the convictions and the point count.

sec13-card-sec13-R03.front: How do ten accumulated points and the two-year window divide roles in a Vermont point suspension?
sec13-card-sec13-R03.expected_back: Ten points is the suspension trigger, while the two year window is what decides how long the suspension lasts.

sec13-card-sec13-F09.front: What determines how long a Vermont point suspension lasts once triggered?
sec13-card-sec13-F09.expected_back: The number of points received within two years determines how long the driving privilege is suspended, and more points mean a longer suspension.

sec13-card-sec13-F01.front: What legal outcome causes points to be added to your Vermont driving record?
sec13-card-sec13-F01.expected_back: Each finding of guilt for breaking a motor vehicle law adds points to your driving record.

sec13-card-sec13-F10.front: Which two categories of vehicle citations carry zero points on a Vermont driving record?
sec13-card-sec13-F10.expected_back: Points are not assessed for parking violations or defective equipment violations.

sec03-card-sec03-F30.front: Who holds the right-of-way when you arrive at an intersection already occupied by walkers, cyclists, or cars?
sec03-card-sec03-F30.expected_back: On every road, pedestrians, bicyclists and other traffic that are already inside an intersection have the right-of-way over a driver arriving at it.

sec03-card-sec03-F31.front: At what pace must you approach a yield sign, and when may you enter the intersection?
sec03-card-sec03-F31.expected_back: Nearing an intersection with a yield right-of-way sign, you must travel slowly enough to stop if necessary and enter only when the way is clear.

sec03-card-sec03-F32.front: Who goes first at a four-way stop, and how is a tie broken when two drivers arrive together?
sec03-card-sec03-F32.expected_back: At a four way stop the first vehicle to arrive has the right-of-way, and when two vehicles arrive at about the same time from different directions the driver on the left yields to the driver on the right.

sec03-card-sec03-R06.front: At a four-way stop, does yielding to the right override the order in which vehicles arrived?
sec03-card-sec03-R06.expected_back: At a four way stop the rule is first to arrive goes first, and only when arrivals are simultaneous does the driver on the left yield to the driver on the right.

sec03-card-sec03-F33.front: Which approaching road users hold the right-of-way over a driver turning left?
sec03-card-sec03-F33.expected_back: A driver turning left must yield to all oncoming traffic, because any vehicle coming toward you, whether a motor vehicle or a bicyclist, has the right-of-way.

sec03-card-sec03-F34.front: Who must yield when pulling out of a driveway, alley, parking lot, or T-intersection stem?
sec03-card-sec03-F34.expected_back: A driver coming onto a road out of a driveway, an alley, a parking lot or the stem of a T intersection gives the right-of-way to every vehicle already traveling on that road.

sec03-card-sec03-F35.front: What two visual checks must happen before entering any intersection?
sec03-card-sec03-F35.expected_back: Before entering any intersection you must search in all directions and make sure you have a clear path through it.

sec03-card-sec03-F27.front: What are the default maximum speed limits on ordinary Vermont roads and on Vermont interstates?
sec03-card-sec03-F27.expected_back: The maximum speed for any vehicle on all Vermont roads is fifty miles per hour or as posted, and on a Vermont interstate the maximum is sixty-five miles per hour or as posted.

sec03-card-sec03-R05.front: How do posted signs interact with the fifty-mile-per-hour road rule and sixty-five interstate rule?
sec03-card-sec03-R05.expected_back: Fifty miles per hour is the maximum on ordinary Vermont roads, while sixty-five miles per hour applies only on the interstate, and both are capped by whatever lower limit is posted.

sec03-card-sec03-F28.front: During which six everyday road, weather, or traffic situations must you drop below the posted speed?
sec03-card-sec03-F28.memory_hook: Corners, curves, crowds, work, weather, walkers
sec03-card-sec03-F28.expected_back: The law requires a vehicle to be under control at all times and driven at a speed that is reasonable for the dangers present, so at intersections, on curves, in heavy traffic, through construction zones, in bad weather and near pedestrians or bicyclists you must slow to a speed safe for conditions.

sec03-card-sec03-F29.front: How low a speed does the handbook warn can still be unsafe when conditions turn treacherous?
sec03-card-sec03-F29.expected_back: Many crashes are caused by driving too fast for conditions, and the handbook warns that even ten miles per hour can sometimes be an unsafe speed.

sec03-card-sec03-F12.front: What minimum distance does Vermont law set for turn signals, and how many seconds match it?
sec03-card-sec03-F12.expected_back: The law requires a turn signal to be given not less than one hundred feet before turning or changing lanes, and signaling three to five seconds ahead satisfies that requirement.

sec03-card-sec03-R02.front: How does Vermont's statutory signal rule in feet connect to the practical counting habit?
sec03-card-sec03-R02.expected_back: The signal law is written as a distance of not less than one hundred feet, while the practical habit is counted as three to five seconds before the turn or lane change.

sec03-card-sec03-F13.front: What must you do immediately if your brake lights or turn-signal lamps stop working?
sec03-card-sec03-F13.expected_back: Pressing the brakes warns drivers behind that you intend to slow or stop, and if the directional or brake lights fail you are required to give hand signals instead and have the lights repaired at once.

sec03-card-sec03-F23.front: What is a visual search pattern, and whom does it help you spot early?
sec03-card-sec03-F23.expected_back: A visual search pattern is an orderly, repeating way of looking for hazards in every direction, including pedestrians, bicyclists and other vulnerable users, so the driver notices changing conditions in and around the intended path.

sec03-card-sec03-F24.front: What baseline following time leaves room for quick stops, and what three conditions call for more?
sec03-card-sec03-F24.expected_back: The four second method leaves enough room to stop quickly behind the vehicle ahead, and when the road is poor, visibility is poor or speeds are higher the gap should grow beyond four seconds.

sec03-card-sec03-F25.front: How do you time your four-second gap against a roadside pole or sign, and what if you arrive early?
sec03-card-sec03-F25.memory_hook: Count from rear bumper, drop back
sec03-card-sec03-F25.expected_back: To measure four second spacing, note when the rear of the vehicle ahead passes a checkpoint such as a sign, driveway, pole or parked vehicle, count seconds until your vehicle reaches it, and fewer than four seconds means you are following too closely and must drop back.

sec03-card-sec03-F26.front: What spoken phrase helps you count true full seconds for following distance?
sec03-card-sec03-F26.expected_back: An easy way to count seconds for following distance is to say one thousand one, one thousand two and so on.

sec03-card-sec03-F15.front: What signal, mirror, left-pass, and lane-choice steps belong when approaching a left turn?
sec03-card-sec03-F15.expected_back: Approaching a left turn, signal three to five seconds in advance, slow gradually while checking the rearview mirror to confirm the driver behind understood, make sure no bicyclist or vehicle behind is trying to pass on your left, and on a multilane road be in the left lane well ahead of the turn without moving suddenly from the right lane.

sec03-card-sec03-F16.front: How close to the centerline should you wait for a left turn, and how must your front wheels point?
sec03-card-sec03-F16.expected_back: At the left turn itself, wait until no vehicles are oncoming, position the vehicle within one foot of the centerline when safe, and keep the wheels straight until you actually turn so a rear end hit will not push you into oncoming traffic.

sec03-card-sec03-R04.front: How does lateral setup distance differ between a left turn and a right turn?
sec03-card-sec03-R04.expected_back: A left turn sets up within one foot of the centerline, whereas a right turn sets up about three feet from the right edge of the road.

sec03-card-sec03-F17.front: Which two groups of road users hold right-of-way over a driver making a left turn?
sec03-card-sec03-F17.expected_back: Any oncoming vehicle or bicyclist has the right-of-way over a left turning driver, and pedestrians crossing the street you are turning into must also be yielded to.

sec03-card-sec03-F18.front: Where relative to the new street's centerline do you finish a left turn, and what comes right after?
sec03-card-sec03-F18.expected_back: Once the road is clear, complete the left turn at a proper speed keeping to the right of the center line, then check the rearview mirror and center the vehicle in its lane.

sec03-card-sec03-F19.front: In what exact three-way order do you scan an intersection right before turning left?
sec03-card-sec03-F19.expected_back: Before a left turn the driver searches the intersection to the right, the front and the left, and enters the new street just to the right of its center line.

sec03-card-sec03-R03.front: How does the intersection scan sequence differ between a left turn and a right turn?
sec03-card-sec03-R03.expected_back: A left turn search runs right, front, left, while a right turn search runs left, front, right and then quickly left again.

sec03-card-sec03-F20.front: How close to the right edge do you set up a right turn, and what steering swing is forbidden?
sec03-card-sec03-F20.memory_hook: Three feet edge, never swing left
sec03-card-sec03-F20.expected_back: On the approach to a right turn keep the vehicle roughly three feet from the road's right edge, never swing out to the left first, and put the signal on three to five seconds ahead while slowing and checking the mirror.

sec03-card-sec03-F21.front: What four-part look sequence and right-side yield apply right before turning right?
sec03-card-sec03-F21.expected_back: Before a right turn the driver searches the intersection left, front, right and then quickly left again, stays alert for bicyclists or pedestrians on the right side, must yield to any of them, and keeps close to the right side of the lane while turning.

sec03-card-sec03-F22.front: Which lane must you enter when turning onto a multilane street, and where do you cruise afterward?
sec03-card-sec03-F22.expected_back: When turning into a street with more than one lane in your direction, turn into the nearest lane, and then follow the multilane rule of driving on the right unless passing or turning.

sec03-card-sec03-F07.front: Before brakes or feet can work, what mental step starts every single stop?
sec03-card-sec03-F07.expected_back: Even with ideal road and vehicle conditions and a fully alert driver, stopping a vehicle takes a great distance, and a stop requires that you see and recognize the danger before anything else happens.

sec03-card-sec03-F08.front: Once you recognize danger, what three links in the chain must happen before the car halts?
sec03-card-sec03-F08.memory_hook: Brain commands, foot presses, brakes grip
sec03-card-sec03-F08.expected_back: After the driver recognizes danger, the brain must tell the foot to brake, the foot must move to the pedal and operate it, and the brakes must work correctly before the vehicle stops.

sec03-card-sec03-F09.front: What does reaction distance measure, and how long does an average driver take to hit the pedal?
sec03-card-sec03-F09.expected_back: Reaction distance is the distance traveled from the moment you see danger until you step on the brake, the average driver needs about three quarters of a second to apply the brakes, and higher speed means more distance covered before braking begins.

sec03-card-sec03-R01.front: Where does reaction distance end and braking distance begin, and which one stretches on slick surfaces?
sec03-card-sec03-R01.memory_hook: Pedal splits them, slick stretches braking
sec03-card-sec03-R01.expected_back: Reaction distance is traveled from seeing danger until stepping on the brake, whereas braking distance is traveled from applying the brakes until stopping and becomes much longer on wet, icy, or gravel roads.

sec03-card-sec03-F10.front: What travel span defines braking distance, and which three surfaces stretch it dramatically?
sec03-card-sec03-F10.memory_hook: Pedal to halt, wet, ice, gravel
sec03-card-sec03-F10.expected_back: Braking distance is the distance traveled from the moment the brakes are applied until the vehicle stops, and it becomes much longer on wet, icy or gravel roads.

sec03-card-sec03-F11.front: Why is pavement slickest during the first few minutes a rainstorm starts?
sec03-card-sec03-F11.memory_hook: Fresh rain floats oil, rubber, dirt
sec03-card-sec03-F11.expected_back: When rain first begins, oil, rubber, dirt and water mix to make the road especially slippery, which increases braking distance.

sec03-card-sec03-F14.front: Why does the handbook highlight left turns in crash statistics?
sec03-card-sec03-F14.expected_back: Many crashes happen while a vehicle is turning left, and most of them would be avoided if the driver made the turn properly.

sec03-card-sec03-F01.front: Does passing the written exam automatically put a learner's permit in your hand?
sec03-card-sec03-F01.expected_back: Passing the written test does not by itself issue a learner's permit; the permit is issued only after every other requirement is met and every required document is provided.

sec03-card-sec03-F02.front: What causes most motor-vehicle crashes, and what three attitudes counter it?
sec03-card-sec03-F02.expected_back: Most motor vehicle crashes are caused by the actions or errors of the driver, and any motorist can drive safely through care, courtesy and caution and by modeling proper behavior.

sec03-card-sec03-F03.front: Where should a brand-new learner's permit holder start practicing behind the wheel?
sec03-card-sec03-F03.expected_back: A new permit holder should begin practicing in an empty parking lot or on lightly traveled roads to build basic car control before moving to busier roads as skills improve.

sec03-card-sec03-F04.front: What does Vermont law require when your slow travel causes traffic to stack up behind you?
sec03-card-sec03-F04.expected_back: When a slow driver has traffic piling up behind, the law requires that driver to move to the roadside once it is safe and let the vehicles behind go past.

sec03-card-sec03-F05.front: Which two clock-face hand grips and turning technique belong on the steering wheel?
sec03-card-sec03-F05.expected_back: Hands belong on the steering wheel at the nine and three or the eight and four clock positions, with hand over hand steering used for turns, while practicing left and right turns, smooth braking and controlled starts and stops.

sec03-card-sec03-F06.front: What six cabin, brake, belt, door, and light steps complete driver readiness before rolling?
sec03-card-sec03-F06.memory_hook: Seat, mirrors, brakes, belt, doors, lights
sec03-card-sec03-F06.expected_back: Driver readiness before moving means adjusting the seat, adjusting all mirrors, testing the foot and parking brakes, adjusting and fastening the safety belt, locking the doors and turning on the headlights.

sec07-card-sec07-F25.front: From which directions is it illegal to pass a stopped school bus displaying flashing red warning lights?
sec07-card-sec07-F25.expected_back: It is against the law to pass a school bus that has stopped with its red warning lights on, from any direction.

sec07-card-sec07-F26.front: What do alternately flashing yellow lights on a slowing school bus tell nearby drivers to do?
sec07-card-sec07-F26.expected_back: When a school bus is about to pick up or drop off students the driver turns on alternately flashing yellow lights and begins slowing, which means you should prepare to stop.

sec07-card-sec07-R02.front: How does your legal duty change when a school bus switches from flashing yellow lights to flashing red?
sec07-card-sec07-R02.expected_back: Alternately flashing yellow lights on a school bus mean prepare to stop, while alternately flashing red lights mean you must be stopped.

sec07-card-sec07-F27.front: Does the duty to stop for a school bus's flashing red lights apply inside a school yard as well as on streets?
sec07-card-sec07-F27.expected_back: Once a stopped school bus activates its alternately flashing red warning lights you must stop your vehicle, and that includes inside a school yard.

sec07-card-sec07-F28.front: Under what opposite-direction roadway setups are you not required to stop for a stopped school bus?
sec07-card-sec07-F28.expected_back: You do not have to stop for a school bus traveling the opposite direction on a divided highway, and a concrete barrier separating traffic from the bus also removes the duty to stop.

sec07-card-sec07-R03.front: Where does the school-bus stop exception apply, and which two common places still require stopping?
sec07-card-sec07-R03.expected_back: The school bus stop exception covers a bus going the other way on a divided highway or behind a concrete barrier, but not a bus on an undivided road and not one inside a school yard.

sec07-card-sec07-F29.front: Passing a stopped school bus displaying red flashers brings what fine and license-point hit in Vermont?
sec07-card-sec07-F29.expected_back: A driver found guilty in Vermont of passing a stopped school bus with its warning lights on faces a substantial fine and five points on the driver's license.

sec07-card-sec07-F33.front: Which road-surface features can force a bicyclist to swerve, requiring drivers to leave maneuvering room?
sec07-card-sec07-F33.expected_back: Drivers should recognize hazards that threaten cyclists, such as potholes, drain grates, railroad tracks and narrow bridges or roads, and give them room to maneuver around them.

sec07-card-sec07-F34.front: How does a bicyclist set up a proper left turn, and what should following motorists let the rider do?
sec07-card-sec07-F34.expected_back: A bicyclist preparing a left turn properly signals and shifts toward the left of the lane or into the turning lane, and drivers should let the rider complete that turn before overtaking.

sec07-card-sec07-F01.front: How should you recover if your wheels drop off the pavement edge onto a low shoulder?
sec07-card-sec07-F01.expected_back: If your wheels drop off the pavement onto a low shoulder, as often happens in construction zones, reduce speed without braking and steer back onto the pavement very carefully at a slow speed.

sec07-card-sec07-F02.front: Which two maneuvers are strictly illegal at a railroad crossing?
sec07-card-sec07-F02.expected_back: It is against the law to drive through, around or under a closed railroad gate, and it is also illegal to pass another vehicle at a railroad crossing.
