sec07-card-sec07-R01.front: How do your duties compare at a closed railroad gate versus an open crossing with warnings or a stop sign?
sec07-card-sec07-R01.expected_back: A closed railroad gate may never be driven through, around or under, while an open crossing still requires a reduced speed and, when lights, a gate, a flagman, a train or a stop sign requires it, a stop at least fifteen feet from the nearest rail.

sec07-card-sec07-F03.front: Whether a rail grade crossing is public or private, how must every motorist approach and cross it?
sec07-card-sec07-F03.expected_back: Every driver must approach and cross any public or private railroad grade crossing at a safe, reduced speed.

sec07-card-sec07-F04.front: How far from the nearest rail must you stop when lights, gates, a flagman, a train, or a stop sign requires it?
sec07-card-sec07-F04.expected_back: By law a driver must stop not less than fifteen feet from the nearest rail when flashing lights, lowered gates or a flagman signal a train, when a train is seen or its whistle heard, or when a stop sign stands at the crossing.

sec07-card-sec07-F05.front: After stopping at a railroad crossing, when may you proceed, and which non-car users must also obey rail signals?
sec07-card-sec07-F05.expected_back: After a required full stop at a crossing the vehicle may cross the tracks when it is safe, and pedestrians, bicyclists and moped riders must also obey railroad warning signals and wait until crossing is safe.

sec07-card-sec07-F06.front: What should you do if you spot a stalled vehicle or dangerous hazard on a railroad crossing?
sec07-card-sec07-F06.expected_back: If a dangerous condition exists at a rail crossing, call the number on the posted emergency sign and give the posted crossing number so the railroad can stop or reroute trains until the hazard is removed.

sec07-card-sec07-F07.front: Which four groups of pedestrians are the most frequent victims of vehicle-pedestrian crashes?
sec07-card-sec07-F07.expected_back: Drivers must watch carefully for pedestrians and be especially alert for young, elderly, disabled or intoxicated pedestrians, who are the most frequent victims of vehicle and pedestrian collisions.

sec07-card-sec07-F08.front: Which mistakes by walkers and by drivers cause pedestrian collisions, and how should motorists adjust?
sec07-card-sec07-F08.expected_back: Many pedestrian crashes come from pedestrians entering traffic carelessly, while others come from drivers failing to yield or failing to use caution, so drive slowly and stay alert wherever pedestrians are present.

sec07-card-sec07-F09.front: If the car ahead stops for a pedestrian on a two-lane-same-way street, may you pass it in the open lane?
sec07-card-sec07-F09.expected_back: When the vehicle ahead stops for a pedestrian, do not pass it even where two lanes are provided, because passing a stopped vehicle is a frequent cause of pedestrian deaths.

sec07-card-sec07-F10.front: Must you still yield to pedestrians who cross against a red light, mid-block, or from between parked cars?
sec07-card-sec07-F10.expected_back: Watch for pedestrians walking against a red light, stepping out from between parked vehicles or crossing where there is no marked crosswalk, and yield to them even when they cross carelessly.

sec07-card-sec07-F11.front: Why must no part of your vehicle sit inside a crosswalk while stopped or waiting to turn?
sec07-card-sec07-F11.expected_back: Never block a crosswalk with any part of the vehicle while stopped or waiting to turn, because that forces pedestrians to walk around you into danger.

sec07-card-sec07-F12.front: When crossing a sidewalk at an alley or driveway, which two walker groups require extra watchfulness?
sec07-card-sec07-F12.expected_back: Look for pedestrians every time your vehicle crosses a sidewalk or shoulder, for instance when pulling into or out of an alley, a driveway or a private road, and take extra care around playing children, who dart without checking traffic, and around elderly walkers, who may not sense the danger.

sec07-card-sec07-F13.front: Is it permissible to stop and pick up hitchhikers along an interstate highway or its ramps?
sec07-card-sec07-F13.expected_back: Do not stop to pick up hitchhikers on the interstate or its ramps.

sec07-card-sec07-F14.front: What exact action must you take when a pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog is crossing or waiting to cross?
sec07-card-sec07-F14.expected_back: A pedestrian who carries a white cane or walks with a guide dog and is crossing, or waiting to cross, the street in front of you requires you to come to a stop and give up the right-of-way.

sec07-card-sec07-R04.front: How does your legal duty toward someone using a white cane or guide dog exceed ordinary pedestrian yielding?
sec07-card-sec07-R04.expected_back: A pedestrian with a white cane or a guide dog requires a full stop and yield, whereas other pedestrians require yielding without necessarily a stop.

sec07-card-sec07-F15.front: What pedestrian and signal rules govern turning at intersections, especially when facing a red arrow?
sec07-card-sec07-F15.expected_back: When turning, look for and yield to pedestrians crossing side streets, many signalized intersections light up no turn on red signs during pedestrian crossing times, and you must never turn right on a red arrow.

sec07-card-sec07-F16.front: What does a pedestrian sign placed right in the roadway at a marked crosswalk remind drivers to do?
sec07-card-sec07-F16.expected_back: At marked crosswalks a pedestrian sign may be placed in the road to remind drivers that they must yield to pedestrians within the crosswalk.

sec07-card-sec07-F30.front: Which Vermont roads may bicyclists legally use, and which traffic rules apply to them?
sec07-card-sec07-F30.expected_back: Bicyclists have the legal right to ride on all roads except where specially prohibited, such as limited access highways like the interstate, and the same traffic rules that apply to vehicle drivers apply to them.

sec07-card-sec07-F31.front: How should you approach and pass a bicycle, and why shouldn't you honk without good reason?
sec07-card-sec07-F31.expected_back: Because bicycles are quieter and less visible, especially at night, a motorist should drive defensively around them, slow down when approaching, give plenty of room when passing, be ready to stop suddenly and not honk without good cause since the noise can startle the rider.

sec07-card-sec07-F32.front: Why is a bicyclist legally allowed to ride toward the center of a lane instead of hugging the edge?
sec07-card-sec07-F32.expected_back: Bicyclists are allowed to ride as far to the left as needed for safety and may take the lane by riding toward its center because of hazards motorists cannot see or to position for the proper travel lane.

sec07-card-sec07-F35.front: What minimum side gap must you leave when passing a bicyclist, and what if the road is too narrow?
sec07-card-sec07-F35.expected_back: When passing a bicyclist keep a gap of at least four feet between the cyclist and your vehicle's right side, and on a road too narrow for the two of you side by side, hold back until you can pass without pushing the rider off the road.

sec07-card-sec07-R05.front: How does your four-foot passing duty interact with a bicyclist's right to occupy a narrow lane?
sec07-card-sec07-R05.expected_back: A driver must leave at least four feet when passing a bicyclist, which is a clearance rule, distinct from the bicyclist's own right to use the whole lane when the road is too narrow to share.

sec07-card-sec07-F36.front: Is it legal for two bicyclists to ride side by side, and how should an approaching driver respond?
sec07-card-sec07-F36.expected_back: Two bicyclists riding side by side are within the law, so reduce speed, let them adjust their position if they choose, and overtake only once it is safe to do so.

sec07-card-sec07-F37.front: How must a left-turning driver treat an oncoming bicyclist, and what speed illusion catches drivers off guard?
sec07-card-sec07-F37.expected_back: An oncoming bicyclist gets the same yield from a left turning driver that an oncoming motorist gets, and riders often travel faster than they seem, so leave them room.

sec07-card-sec07-F38.front: What four everyday driver mistakes most commonly strike bicyclists?
sec07-card-sec07-F38.expected_back: Four common driver errors strike bicyclists: turning left without yielding to an oncoming cyclist, turning right without checking for a cyclist on the right going straight or leaving a sidewalk, entering or crossing a street without checking for a cyclist, and opening a door into a cyclist's path.

sec07-card-sec07-F17.front: What three things must you stay alert for whenever signs or flashing lights mark a school zone?
sec07-card-sec07-F17.expected_back: Be alert at all times for children, pedestrians and arriving or departing school buses in a school zone, where signs or flashing lights warn of the school or crossing.

sec07-card-sec07-F18.front: When do reduced school-zone speed limits apply, and why must you still watch outside weekday class hours?
sec07-card-sec07-F18.expected_back: Many school zones post lower speed limits that apply when flashing or when children are present, as the sign states, and children are present after school and on weekends, not only during regular school hours.

sec07-card-sec07-F19.front: Why must you take extra care in residential neighborhoods, especially when backing in or out of a driveway?
sec07-card-sec07-F19.expected_back: In residential areas and wherever children are likely, be extra careful, teach your own children pedestrian rights and duties early, and always be extra watchful when backing in or out of a driveway because children may run or play behind the vehicle.

sec07-card-sec07-F20.front: What legal duty stops a pedestrian from stepping off a curb straight in front of a close vehicle?
sec07-card-sec07-F20.expected_back: Although drivers must yield to pedestrians, a pedestrian must not suddenly leave a curb or other safe place and walk into the path of a vehicle so close that it is an immediate hazard, because vehicles cannot stop at once.

sec07-card-sec07-F21.front: How should a pedestrian respond to a flashing Don't Walk signal if still on the curb versus already crossing?
sec07-card-sec07-F21.expected_back: Pedestrians should look both ways before crossing, obey walk and don't walk signs, not start to cross on a flashing don't walk, and may finish a crossing begun on walk during the flashing phase.

sec07-card-sec07-F22.front: Where no pedestrian signals exist, on which traffic light should a walker cross, and what danger remains?
sec07-card-sec07-F22.expected_back: Facing a yellow or red light a pedestrian should not cross unless a walk sign shows, and where there are no pedestrian signals the pedestrian crosses when the light turns green for traffic moving the same way while watching for turning vehicles.

sec07-card-sec07-F23.front: When a road has no sidewalk, which side and direction must a pedestrian use?
sec07-card-sec07-F23.expected_back: Pedestrians should use sidewalks where they exist, and where there are none should walk as far to the left as possible facing traffic, never on the right with their back to traffic.

sec07-card-sec07-R06.front: On a road without sidewalks, how does a pedestrian's road side compare with a bicyclist's?
sec07-card-sec07-R06.expected_back: A pedestrian without a sidewalk walks on the left facing traffic, the opposite of a bicyclist, who rides on the right with traffic.

sec07-card-sec07-F24.front: What clothing, light, and headphone habits keep pedestrians safer, especially from dusk through dawn?
sec07-card-sec07-F24.expected_back: Pedestrians should use crosswalks, which exist to concentrate crossings where they can be made safely, and at dawn, dusk or night should wear light colored or reflective clothing and carry a light, and should not wear headphones in busy areas so they can hear traffic.

sec07-card-sec07-F39.front: Do bicyclists need a license, when may they ride two abreast, and can they receive traffic tickets?
sec07-card-sec07-F39.expected_back: Bicyclists hold every right and duty of a vehicle driver without needing a license, must follow all rules of the road, may ride two abreast provided normal traffic flow is not held up, and can be ticketed and fined for traffic violations.

sec07-card-sec07-F40.front: How should a bicyclist ride past parked cars, handle right-turn lanes when going straight, and signal turns?
sec07-card-sec07-F40.expected_back: A bicyclist rides with traffic on the right, stays out of a right turn lane when going straight, holds a predictable straight line instead of weaving among parked cars, may hold a narrow lane until moving right is safe, and signals turns by hand after checking the lanes are clear.

sec10-card-sec10-F08.front: How should you use your eyes, mirrors, and following count on a Vermont interstate?
sec10-card-sec10-F08.expected_back: On the interstate keep your eyes moving to know what is happening around you, check the mirrors often, and avoid tailgating by using the four second rule with extra space on wet or slippery roads.

sec10-card-sec10-F09.front: How should you communicate and check before changing lanes or passing on the interstate?
sec10-card-sec10-F09.expected_back: Let other drivers know what you will do before you do it, never slow down or change lanes suddenly, treat frequent lane changes as unsafe, and before changing lanes or passing check the mirrors, signal and check the blind spot on the side you will move to.

sec10-card-sec10-F10.front: When is stopping legal on an interstate, and how do you position and signal for help?
sec10-card-sec10-F10.expected_back: Never stop in an interstate traffic lane; stopping on an interstate is illegal except in an emergency, and then you move into the breakdown lane as far right as possible, raise the hood, tie a white cloth on the vehicle and stay inside if you need help.

sec10-card-sec10-F11.front: Which lane should you normally travel in on a Vermont interstate?
sec10-card-sec10-F11.expected_back: Drive in the right lane of the interstate unless you are passing another vehicle or a sign directs otherwise.

sec10-card-sec10-F12.front: Why must you avoid driving tired on the interstate, and what should you do if drowsiness hits?
sec10-card-sec10-F12.expected_back: Do not drive when tired, since fatigue is a major cause of interstate crashes, and if you become tired stop and rest in a safe area as soon as possible.

sec10-card-sec10-F14.front: What must you do after missing an interstate exit, and which two shortcuts are illegal?
sec10-card-sec10-F14.expected_back: If you miss your exit never stop and back up and never use the emergency turnaround, which is reserved for emergency and maintenance vehicles; go on to the next exit.

sec10-card-sec10-R03.front: Which one lawful option replaces backing up or using a median crossover after missing an exit?
sec10-card-sec10-R03.expected_back: A missed exit is handled by continuing to the next one, never by backing up on the interstate and never by using the emergency crossover.

sec10-card-sec10-F15.front: In which four weather or surface conditions must you never engage cruise control?
sec10-card-sec10-F15.memory_hook: Never use rain, fog, snow, ice
sec10-card-sec10-F15.expected_back: Never use cruise control in conditions such as rain, fog, snow or ice.

sec10-card-sec10-F16.front: How must you pass a stopped police, emergency, or repair vehicle displaying flashing lights?
sec10-card-sec10-F16.expected_back: When a police, emergency or repair vehicle sits at the roadside with a flashing light, you must slow down, continue with caution and move a lane away from it as soon as that is safe, and if no lane change is possible you must pass at twenty miles per hour under the speed limit.

sec10-card-sec10-R02.front: When does Vermont's twenty-mile-per-hour-under rule apply past a stopped emergency vehicle instead of changing lanes?
sec10-card-sec10-R02.expected_back: Passing a stopped emergency vehicle on the interstate requires a lane change where safe, and only when no lane change is possible does the rule become slowing to twenty miles per hour under the limit.

sec10-card-sec10-F18.front: What sequence of checks and signals comes before pulling left to pass a vehicle or bicycle?
sec10-card-sec10-F18.expected_back: To pass a vehicle or bicycle ahead, make sure you have enough distance, signal left, look to the rear in the mirrors and over your left shoulder to check whether you are being passed, then change lanes and pass on the left.

sec10-card-sec10-F22.front: What side clearance is required when overtaking on the left, and when may you merge back right?
sec10-card-sec10-F22.expected_back: Overtake vehicles and bicycles on the left with at least four feet of clearance, stay out until the whole front of the vehicle or the bicyclist shows in your inside rearview mirror, then signal right, glance over your right shoulder at the blind spot and move back to the right.

sec10-card-sec10-F23.front: What two courteous adjustments should you make while another driver passes you?
sec10-card-sec10-F23.expected_back: When another vehicle is passing you, slow a little and keep right so the other driver can pass more safely.

sec10-card-sec10-F24.front: In which two roadway situations may a Vermont driver pass on the right?
sec10-card-sec10-F24.expected_back: A driver may pass on the right on a multilane road, and on other roads may pass on the right of a vehicle or bicycle that is turning or preparing to turn left when there is room to go by safely.

sec10-card-sec10-R04.front: What strict surface boundary separates a legal right-side pass from an illegal one?
sec10-card-sec10-R04.expected_back: Passing on the right is lawful on a multilane road or beside a vehicle turning left, but never by leaving the pavement or the main traveled part of the road.

sec10-card-sec10-F25.front: Under what circumstances may you drive off the pavement or main traveled road to pass?
sec10-card-sec10-F25.expected_back: Under no conditions may a vehicle be passed by driving off the pavement or off the main traveled part of the road.

sec10-card-sec10-F26.front: At which five road features or sign zones is passing strictly prohibited?
sec10-card-sec10-F26.expected_back: Do not pass on hills, on curves, at railroad crossings, at intersections or where a changed path ahead sign appears.

sec10-card-sec10-F02.front: How are interstates built, and what six other names do regions use for free or tolled highways?
sec10-card-sec10-F02.expected_back: Interstates are multiple lane divided roads built for high speed travel, known elsewhere as expressways, throughways, turnpikes, toll roads, limited access highways or freeways, some free and some tolled.

sec10-card-sec10-F03.front: What travel benefit comes from an interstate's multi-lane, controlled-access layout?
sec10-card-sec10-F03.expected_back: Interstates are multi lane, controlled access roads on which you can drive very long distances without interruption, designed for quicker and safer travel, so learning to use them properly matters.

sec10-card-sec10-F04.front: Where do speed-change lanes run, and how do they connect ramps with interstate travel lanes?
sec10-card-sec10-F04.expected_back: Speed change lanes run alongside the interstate for a short distance to connect entrance or exit ramps with the travel lanes and let vehicles speed up or slow down when entering or leaving.

sec10-card-sec10-F05.front: What five-step sequence takes you smoothly from an entrance ramp onto the interstate?
sec10-card-sec10-F05.memory_hook: Stay right, signal, accelerate, check, merge
sec10-card-sec10-F05.expected_back: An entrance ramp is a short one way road onto the interstate that leads to the acceleration lane, where you stay right, signal left, speed up to interstate speed, check the blind spot over the left shoulder and change lanes when the travel lane is safe.

sec10-card-sec10-R01.front: How does speed timing differ between an interstate entrance ramp and an exit ramp?
sec10-card-sec10-R01.expected_back: On an entrance ramp the entering driver speeds up and yields to interstate traffic, while on an exit ramp the driver slows only after reaching the deceleration lane.

sec10-card-sec10-F06.front: Who must yield when a vehicle enters the interstate from a ramp?
sec10-card-sec10-F06.expected_back: A driver entering the interstate must yield to drivers already on it.

sec10-card-sec10-F07.front: What three steps take you cleanly off the interstate onto an exit ramp?
sec10-card-sec10-F07.expected_back: An exit ramp is a short one way road connecting the interstate to another road, and to leave you signal for a lane change, move into the deceleration lane nearest the exit and slow to the posted exit speed.

sec10-card-sec10-F01.front: Where should you aim your eyes against bright oncoming headlights, and what bonus hazard does it spot?
sec10-card-sec10-F01.expected_back: To avoid being blinded by oncoming headlights look ahead toward the right edge of the highway until the bright lights pass and your vision returns, a habit that also helps you spot bicyclists or pedestrians near the road edge.

sec10-card-sec10-F13.front: Why do snowy or icy interstates, ramps, bridges, and overpasses demand extra speed reductions?
sec10-card-sec10-F13.expected_back: Icy and snow covered interstates and their ramps are very dangerous, so slow down and drive with care, remembering that bridges and overpasses may be more slippery than the main road.

sec10-card-sec10-F17.front: What does seeing a yellow edge line on your right side along a divided highway mean?
sec10-card-sec10-F17.expected_back: If the edge line to your right on a divided highway is painted yellow you are going the wrong way, because on a divided highway or interstate the line on your right should be white.

sec10-card-sec10-R05.front: Which edge-line color belongs on your right on an interstate, and what warns you of wrong-way travel?
sec10-card-sec10-R05.expected_back: On a divided highway or interstate, a yellow edge line on your right warns that you are going the wrong way, because the line to your right should be white.

sec10-card-sec10-F19.front: How can you alert a driver ahead of your intention to pass at night?
sec10-card-sec10-F19.expected_back: At night it may be necessary to flick the headlights from low to high to low to warn the driver ahead that you intend to pass.

sec10-card-sec10-F20.front: What extra precaution is vital before returning right after passing while towing a trailer?
sec10-card-sec10-F20.expected_back: When passing while towing a trailer be especially sure you are well past the vehicle or bicycle before pulling back into its lane.

sec10-card-sec10-F21.front: When must you take extra side-clearance care around motorists and bicyclists while passing?
sec10-card-sec10-F21.expected_back: When towing a wide load or driving an unusually wide vehicle be especially careful when passing any motorist or bicyclist.

sec08-card-sec08-F13.front: How should you think of a moving motorcycle, and which manual covers motorcycle permits and endorsements?
sec08-card-sec08-F13.expected_back: When a motorcycle is in motion, think of it as a person rather than as a machine, and consult the Vermont Motorcycle Manual for motorcycle laws and how to get a motorcycle permit or endorsement.

sec08-card-sec08-F14.front: In over seventy percent of fatal car-truck crashes, which driver caused the wreck, and in what weather?
sec08-card-sec08-F14.expected_back: Each year more than two hundred fifty thousand crashes involve passenger vehicles and large trucks, in more than seventy percent of fatal car and truck crashes the driver of the other vehicle rather than the truck driver caused the crash, and most of these crashes happen in daylight on straight, dry pavement in good weather.

sec08-card-sec08-F15.front: In four out of every five fatal collisions involving a large truck, who is the person killed?
sec08-card-sec08-F15.expected_back: The handbook states that the person killed in four of every five fatal truck crashes is the driver of the other vehicle, and that understanding truck limitations would let motorists avoid many of them.

sec08-card-sec08-F16.front: Which four driving demands expand as a truck gets larger?
sec08-card-sec08-F16.expected_back: The bigger the truck, the bigger the driver's blind spots, the more room it needs to maneuver, the longer it takes to stop, and the longer it takes you to pass it.

sec08-card-sec08-F17.front: Where sit a large truck's no-zones, and what simple mirror check tells you whether the driver can see you?
sec08-card-sec08-F17.expected_back: Large trucks have blind spots called no-zones around the front, back and sides, a truck could turn into a vehicle hidden there, and if you cannot see the truck's side mirrors the truck driver cannot see you.

sec08-card-sec08-F18.front: When overtaking a large truck, what must appear in your inside rearview mirror before you merge back right?
sec08-card-sec08-F18.expected_back: Passing a large truck takes longer, so keep a steady speed and make sure you can see the truck's cab in your inside rearview mirror before returning to the right lane, because pulling in front of a truck too soon may force its driver to act quickly to avoid a crash.

sec08-card-sec08-F19.front: Why must you wait patiently instead of driving around a truck that is backing or setting up to back?
sec08-card-sec08-F19.expected_back: A truck driver backing up may have to block the street temporarily to maneuver the trailer, and you must never go around a truck that is preparing to back or is backing, because trailers hide objects and you would enter a blind spot.

sec08-card-sec08-F20.front: What two visibility losses make following closely right behind a large truck so hazardous?
sec08-card-sec08-F20.expected_back: Trucks have long blind spots directly behind them where the driver cannot see you and your own view of traffic is badly reduced, so following too closely greatly raises the chance of a rear end collision with the truck.

sec08-card-sec08-R03.front: How does the crash risk in a truck's rear no-zone differ from lingering in its side no-zones?
sec08-card-sec08-R03.expected_back: A truck's rear no-zone hides you from the driver and hides traffic from you, while its side no-zones are where a sudden truck lane change can hit you; the mirror test applies to both.

sec08-card-sec08-F21.front: Why is lingering alongside either side of a large truck far riskier than driving beside a passenger car?
sec08-card-sec08-F21.expected_back: Trucks have much larger blind spots on both sides than passenger vehicles, and lingering in them means the truck driver cannot see you, so a sudden lane change by the truck could cause a serious crash.

sec08-card-sec08-F22.front: Why do trucks often swing left before turning right, and what curb mistake must drivers never make?
sec08-card-sec08-F22.expected_back: Truck drivers often swing wide to the left to make a right turn and cannot see vehicles directly behind or beside them, so always watch a truck's turn signals and never cut in between the truck and the curb or shoulder on the right.

sec08-card-sec08-F02.front: How do a motorcyclist's highway rights compare with a car driver's, and what restraint applies to both sides?
sec08-card-sec08-F02.expected_back: A motorcyclist has the same rights and responsibilities on the highway as any other driver, so motorists must not crowd motorcycles or take the right-of-way from them, while riders in turn must not exploit the cycle's narrow profile and maneuverability.

sec08-card-sec08-F03.front: Why must you keep more than four seconds behind a motorcycle, especially approaching intersections?
sec08-card-sec08-F03.expected_back: Motorcyclists often slow by downshifting or rolling off the throttle without lighting the brake lamp, so allow more than four seconds of following distance and expect a rider to slow at an intersection without visible warning.

sec08-card-sec08-F04.front: Why shouldn't you pull out immediately just because an approaching motorcycle's turn signal is blinking?
sec08-card-sec08-F04.expected_back: Motorcycle turn signals usually do not cancel themselves, so a rider, especially a beginner, may leave one flashing after a turn or lane change, and a driver should confirm that a motorcycle's signal is real before acting on it.

sec08-card-sec08-F05.front: Why do smart motorcyclists move left, center, or right within their lane during normal riding?
sec08-card-sec08-F05.expected_back: Motorcyclists shift position within a lane on purpose, to be seen more easily and to reduce the effects of wind, road debris and passing vehicles, not to be reckless or show off.

sec08-card-sec08-F06.front: How does a motorcycle's slim outline trick your eyes on speed and distance before an intersection turn?
sec08-card-sec08-F06.expected_back: A motorcycle's small size makes it appear to travel faster than its true speed and to sit farther away than it really is, so a driver checking traffic before turning at an intersection should assume the motorcycle is closer than it looks.

sec08-card-sec08-R01.front: Given how a small silhouette distorts speed and range, what safe assumption should guide intersection turns?
sec08-card-sec08-R01.expected_back: A motorcycle looks farther away and faster than it is, so the safe assumption at an intersection is that it is closer and no faster than it appears.

sec08-card-sec08-F07.front: Behind which everyday cabin and roadside objects can an entire motorcycle disappear from view?
sec08-card-sec08-F07.expected_back: A motorcycle's small size lets it hide behind door posts, mirrors, passengers, bushes, trees, parked cars, fences, bridges and blind spots, so take an extra moment to check traffic thoroughly before changing lanes or turning.

sec08-card-sec08-F08.front: How does a motorcycle's stopping distance compare with a car's, and what happens on slick pavement?
sec08-card-sec08-F08.expected_back: A motorcycle's stopping distance is nearly the same as a car's, but slippery pavement makes a quick stop hard, so allow extra following distance because a motorcycle cannot always stop on a dime.

sec08-card-sec08-F09.front: Why shouldn't you count on a motorcycle swerving clear, especially when a second rider is aboard?
sec08-card-sec08-F09.expected_back: Maneuverability is a motorcycle strength at slower speeds on good roads, but a driver must not expect the rider to always dodge out of the way, and a passenger makes balance harder, lengthens stopping distance and reduces maneuverability, especially near intersections.

sec08-card-sec08-F10.front: How do a motorcycle's small convex mirrors distort your car's reflection, and what gap should you hold?
sec08-card-sec08-F10.expected_back: Motorcycle mirrors are smaller and usually convex, which shows the rider a smaller image of your vehicle that appears farther back than it is, so keep at least a four second space cushion when following a motorcycle.

sec08-card-sec08-F11.front: Why do motorists unintentionally overlook motorcycles, and what visual clue matters after dark?
sec08-card-sec08-F11.expected_back: Because cars and trucks far outnumber motorcycles some drivers fail to recognize a motorcycle and ignore it unintentionally, so look for motorcycles when checking traffic at intersections, and at night remember that single headlights or taillights blending into traffic may be a motorcycle.

sec08-card-sec08-F12.front: How must you change lanes and use speed when passing a motorcycle or being passed by one?
sec08-card-sec08-F12.expected_back: A motorcycle is entitled to a full lane, so pass it by changing lanes completely, never cut back in too closely after overtaking, use turn signals to tell the rider you intend to pass, change lanes or turn, and never speed up to stay ahead of a motorcycle that is passing you.

sec08-card-sec08-R02.front: What key rule defines passing a motorcycle compared with returning to your lane ahead of a truck?
sec08-card-sec08-R02.expected_back: Passing a motorcycle means changing lanes completely because it owns a full lane, whereas passing a truck means waiting until its whole cab shows in your inside mirror before returning.

sec08-card-sec08-F29.front: What road rights do animal riders and animal-drawn vehicles hold, and how must an approaching driver react?
sec08-card-sec08-F29.expected_back: A person riding an animal or driving an animal drawn vehicle on a public highway has all the rights of a motor vehicle driver, and a motorist meeting one must reduce speed and possibly stop to avoid frightening the animal and to protect the rider or driver.

sec08-card-sec08-F30.front: What noise ban, lane rule, and following cushion apply around ridden horses, wagons, or herded livestock?
sec08-card-sec08-F30.expected_back: Never blow the horn or rev the engine, especially on a motorcycle, when meeting, following or passing animals, use the full traffic lane to pass completely without cutting back quickly, and leave at least four seconds behind a ridden horse, a horse and wagon or herded animals.

sec08-card-sec08-R05.front: How does Vermont's rule around horses and livestock compare with handling an aggressive driver?
sec08-card-sec08-R05.expected_back: Around animals the rule is silence and distance, no horn and no revving with four seconds behind, whereas around an aggressive driver the rule is calm avoidance without retaliation.

sec08-card-sec08-F31.front: What legal penalties can hit a motorist who operates negligently around animals on a Vermont highway?
sec08-card-sec08-F31.expected_back: A motor vehicle operator may be fined or imprisoned for negligent operation around animals on the highway.

sec08-card-sec08-F23.front: What rear emblem identifies tractors and slow farm machinery, and how does spotting it help you?
sec08-card-sec08-F23.expected_back: A slow moving vehicle such as a tractor or large farm machinery cannot travel at highway speed and carries an orange and red triangular emblem on its rear so motorists recognize it sooner and have more time to slow down.

sec08-card-sec08-R04.front: Which colors and shape mounted on the back identify slow-moving farm equipment?
sec08-card-sec08-R04.expected_back: Slow-moving equipment like a tractor or large farm machinery displays a rear-mounted orange-and-red triangular emblem.

sec08-card-sec08-F24.front: Which three width, visibility, and turning surprises make passing farm equipment tricky?
sec08-card-sec08-F24.expected_back: Farm vehicles can swing wide into unmarked field entrances on either side of the road, some equipment is wider than the road, and swaying wagons or implements can hide the operator from view.

sec08-card-sec08-F25.front: What road right do agricultural operators hold, and why keep four seconds or more behind them?
sec08-card-sec08-F25.expected_back: A slow moving vehicle that delays traffic may pull over when it is possible and safe to let others pass, agricultural operators have a right to use the road, and you should keep a safe following distance, possibly more than four seconds, so that you and the operator can see each other.

sec08-card-sec08-F26.front: How should you handle oncoming wide farm machinery on narrow roads, and when may you pass?
sec08-card-sec08-F26.expected_back: Yield to wide equipment on narrow roads, pass slow moving vehicles cautiously only when conditions are safe and no traffic is oncoming, and stay patient and alert for turning vehicles.

sec08-card-sec08-F32.front: During which three daily periods do moose and deer roam and feed most actively near posted crossings?
sec08-card-sec08-F32.expected_back: A collision with a moose or deer can kill the driver and passengers as well as the animal, so drive cautiously where deer and moose crossing signs are posted, especially in late evening, at night and in early morning when the animals roam and feed.

sec08-card-sec08-F33.front: How can headlights make a deer react, how fast can it bolt, and why look for another?
sec08-card-sec08-F33.expected_back: Headlights may freeze a deer in place or send it bounding at up to forty miles per hour toward its habitat, so a deer on the far side of the road from its habitat may bolt in front of you, and animals travel in pairs so expect a second one after the first.

sec08-card-sec08-F34.front: What two physical traits make hitting a moose far deadlier for car occupants than hitting a deer?
sec08-card-sec08-F34.expected_back: Moose collisions are deadlier because a moose weighs more than a thousand pounds and stands much taller than a deer, so it can land on top of the vehicle with crushing force.

sec08-card-sec08-F35.front: Why are moose much harder to spot in headlights at dusk than deer?
sec08-card-sec08-F35.expected_back: Deer eyes reflect headlights, but a moose stands so tall that its eyes may not reflect and it is more darkly colored than a deer, which makes moose especially hard to see in the evening.

sec08-card-sec08-R06.front: Why do deer eyes glow back in car headlights while a moose's eyes usually do not?
sec08-card-sec08-R06.expected_back: Deer eyes shine in headlights but a moose's usually do not because of its height and dark color, which is why moose are the harder animal to spot at dusk.

sec08-card-sec08-F01.front: Why do skateboarders, rollerbladers, kick-scooter riders, and electric-wheelchair users demand extra caution?
sec08-card-sec08-F01.expected_back: Skateboarders, roller bladers, nonmotorized scooter riders and electric wheelchair users can travel at significant speed, move abruptly and change direction unexpectedly into your path, so drivers must be especially alert and cautious around them.

sec08-card-sec08-F27.front: Which unlawful driving habits and hostile gestures mark an aggressive driver?
sec08-card-sec08-F27.expected_back: Aggressive drivers drive too fast, pass unsafely, skip signals for lane changes, weave through traffic, follow too closely and cut off cars, all of which is unlawful and can bring tickets or worse, and they may also yell, honk and flash their lights.

sec08-card-sec08-F28.front: What is the smart, safe response when an aggressive driver cuts you off or drives dangerously?
sec08-card-sec08-F28.expected_back: When an aggressive driver cuts you off or acts unsafely, the right response is to keep calm, move out of that driver's way, avoid any challenge and never attempt to get even.

sec14-card-sec14-F21.front: What coverage must any vehicle you drive carry under Vermont's financial responsibility law, and why?
sec14-card-sec14-F21.expected_back: Vermont's maintenance of financial responsibility law requires the vehicle you drive to be covered by liability insurance, and liability and property damage coverage protect you from financial loss when bodily injury or property damage occurs.

sec14-card-sec14-F22.front: What three minimum dollar amounts are required for Vermont motor-vehicle liability insurance?
sec14-card-sec14-F22.expected_back: Coverage must be at least twenty-five thousand dollars for death or injury of one person, fifty thousand dollars for death or injury of two or more persons and ten thousand dollars for property damage.

sec14-card-sec14-R02.front: Which loss category matches twenty-five thousand, fifty thousand, and ten thousand dollars in Vermont coverage?
sec14-card-sec14-R02.expected_back: Twenty-five thousand dollars covers one person's death or injury, fifty thousand covers two or more people, and ten thousand covers property damage.

sec14-card-sec14-F23.front: Where must your insurer's proof card stay, and during which two occasions must you present it?
sec14-card-sec14-F23.expected_back: You must carry an insurance card from your insurer in the vehicle showing the vehicle is covered, and must show it when stopped by a police officer and when taking a driving test.

sec14-card-sec14-F24.front: What happens if stopped completely uninsured versus insured without the paper card on hand?
sec14-card-sec14-F24.expected_back: A driver stopped without insurance receives a ticket, a fine and two points on the driving record, while an insured driver who cannot show the card at the stop has fifteen days to produce a card proving coverage at the time of the stop.

sec14-card-sec14-R03.front: How does Vermont's roadside penalty separate an uninsured driver from an insured driver missing the card?
sec14-card-sec14-R03.expected_back: Being uninsured at a stop earns a ticket, fine and two points, whereas being insured but cardless earns fifteen days to produce the card.

sec14-card-sec14-F25.front: When does driving uninsured cost your license, and how long must future insurance proof stay filed?
sec14-card-sec14-F25.expected_back: Driving without insurance and then having a crash even if not at fault, driving under the influence, taking a vehicle without consent, driving while suspended, revoked or refused, causing a death or leaving a crash scene costs you the license until you get insurance, with proof required for a full three years.

sec14-card-sec14-F01.front: Who must register road vehicles in Vermont, and what deadline applies after moving from out of state?
sec14-card-sec14-F01.expected_back: A Vermont resident must register any vehicle driven on the roads, and a person moving in from another state must register the vehicle within sixty days of moving into Vermont.

sec14-card-sec14-R01.front: Compare Vermont's deadlines for new-resident registration, mailing vehicle-trade paperwork, and reporting personal or color updates?
sec14-card-sec14-R01.memory_hook: Sixty newcomer, twenty-four trade, thirty change
sec14-card-sec14-R01.expected_back: A new resident has sixty days to register a vehicle, while a sale paperwork package after a trade must be mailed within twenty-four hours and a name, address or color change must be reported within thirty days.

sec14-card-sec14-F02.front: Where must valid registration proof stay whenever a vehicle is driven, and who can inspect it?
sec14-card-sec14-F02.expected_back: Proof of valid registration must always be in the vehicle while it is in use and a police officer has the right to see it.

sec14-card-sec14-F03.front: How must Vermont plates be fastened and maintained, and from how far must rear lighting make them readable?
sec14-card-sec14-F03.expected_back: Registration plates must be firmly attached so they cannot loosen, no part may be covered or hidden, they must be kept clean, and the rear plate must be lit so it can be read from at least fifty feet away.

sec14-card-sec14-F04.front: Can you share plates across cars you own, and when may old plates move onto another purchase?
sec14-card-sec14-F04.expected_back: The number plates issued for a vehicle may be used only on that vehicle, but you may transfer them to a new vehicle you buy when you trade in or sell the old one.

sec14-card-sec14-F10.front: Which three owner or vehicle changes must you report to the Vermont DMV within thirty days?
sec14-card-sec14-F10.expected_back: A change of your name, your address or the color of your vehicle must be reported to the DMV within thirty days.

sec14-card-sec14-F05.front: What paperwork details and plate step must a seller complete when selling a vehicle?
sec14-card-sec14-F05.expected_back: When selling a vehicle give the buyer a bill of sale with the buyer's name, the seller's signature, the date, and the vehicle's year, make, serial number and sale price, sign the back of the title with the new owner's name and address, the mileage and the date, and remove your plates.

sec14-card-sec14-F06.front: Which vehicle model years require a buyer-and-seller signed odometer statement upon sale, and where does it appear?
sec14-card-sec14-F06.expected_back: An odometer statement signed by both seller and buyer is required on every sale of a vehicle of model year twenty eleven or newer, and the statement is part of the title or the Vermont bill of sale.

sec14-card-sec14-F07.front: What paperwork, plate step, and Montpelier mailing deadline apply when trading vehicles?
sec14-card-sec14-F07.expected_back: When trading vehicles exchange bills of sale, have the title to the vehicle you receive signed over to you, remove your plates from the old vehicle and put them on the new one if you transfer the registration, and mail the registration, tax and title application with the title and fees to the DMV in Montpelier within twenty-four hours.

sec14-card-sec14-F08.front: Through which three channels can you replace a lost Vermont registration certificate?
sec14-card-sec14-F08.expected_back: A lost registration certificate can be replaced at any DMV office, by mail or online.

sec14-card-sec14-F09.front: Where can you obtain a Replacement Plate Application if one or both plates go missing?
sec14-card-sec14-F09.expected_back: If one or both registration plates are lost, a Replacement Plate Application is available at any DMV office, at a police station or online.

sec14-card-sec14-F11.front: How is Vermont's six-percent purchase and use tax calculated on a bought, non-leased vehicle?
sec14-card-sec14-F11.expected_back: Buying a new or used non leased vehicle triggers the purchase and use tax of six percent of the price paid or the current fair market value, whichever is greater.

sec14-card-sec14-R04.front: How does Vermont's six-percent tax base differ between buying a vehicle outright and leasing one?
sec14-card-sec14-R04.expected_back: The purchase and use tax is six percent of the higher of price or fair market value for a purchase, but six percent of acquisition cost minus lease end value for a lease.

sec14-card-sec14-F12.front: Under what two conditions is a newcomer's previously owned out-of-state vehicle exempt from Vermont purchase tax?
sec14-card-sec14-F12.expected_back: A new resident registering a vehicle acquired outside Vermont on which they or their spouse already paid a sales or use tax is exempt from the Vermont tax when the tax paid elsewhere equals or exceeds Vermont's, or when the vehicle was registered for at least three years in a jurisdiction that collects such a tax, and otherwise owes the difference.

sec14-card-sec14-F13.front: Which documents verify lease tax on a Vermont-dealer lease, and what happens if none accompany registration?
sec14-card-sec14-F13.expected_back: A leased vehicle from a Vermont dealer must be registered with a purchase and use tax computation form or the lease agreement or dealer worksheet, and without them the vehicle is taxed at six percent of the acquisition cost.

sec14-card-sec14-F14.front: How is taxable cost figured on a documented lease, and does a buyout option change it?
sec14-card-sec14-F14.expected_back: The taxable cost of a leased vehicle is six percent of the acquisition cost minus the lease end value as stated in the computation form, lease agreement or dealer worksheet, regardless of whether there is an option to buy at lease end.

sec14-card-sec14-F15.front: Which motorcycles and trailers are exempt from Vermont's general motor-vehicle title requirement?
sec14-card-sec14-F15.expected_back: Every vehicle must have a Vermont motor vehicle title, with exceptions such as a motorcycle under three hundred cubic centimeters of engine displacement and a trailer with an empty weight of fifteen hundred pounds or less.

sec14-card-sec14-F16.front: Which special document is mandatory to register a brand-new vehicle alongside standard Vermont registration papers?
sec14-card-sec14-F16.expected_back: A Manufacturer's Certificate of Origin is required for every new vehicle and no new vehicle can be registered without it, and any vehicle registered in Vermont needs a registration application, the bill of sale and the former owner's title signed over.

sec14-card-sec14-F17.front: What makes up a modern vehicle identification number, and when did seventeen characters become standard?
sec14-card-sec14-F17.expected_back: A vehicle identification number is a unique seventeen character code of digits and capital letters that identifies a specific vehicle and its features, specifications and manufacturer, and before nineteen eighty-one such numbers varied from eleven to seventeen characters.

sec14-card-sec14-R06.front: All post-nineteen-eighty-one cars carry seventeen-character codes, so which three registration categories require physical verification?
sec14-card-sec14-R06.expected_back: A seventeen character identification number is standard since nineteen eighty-one, and verification of it is required only for salvage, bonded title and foreign registered vehicles.

sec14-card-sec14-F18.front: Which three vehicle types need identification-number verification, and who in Vermont may perform it?
sec14-card-sec14-F18.expected_back: Vehicle identification number verification is required for vehicles with salvage documentation, vehicles being titled under bond and vehicles registered in any foreign country including Canada, and it must be done in Vermont by a law enforcement officer, supervised law enforcement personnel or a designated DMV employee.

sec14-card-sec14-F19.front: How is a Vermont title branded after registering a salvage vehicle, and what check comes first?
sec14-card-sec14-F19.expected_back: A vehicle registered in Vermont with a salvage title receives a title marked rebuilt vehicle, and registering it requires having the identification number checked by a DMV employee or Vermont law enforcement with the verification section of the application completed.

sec14-card-sec14-F20.front: What does a car loan place on your vehicle, and who keeps the title until payoff?
sec14-card-sec14-F20.expected_back: Borrowing money from a bank, credit union or another person to buy a vehicle puts a lien on it, the lender is the lien holder whose name must be on the registration application, and the title is sent to the lien holder and withheld from you until the loan is repaid.

sec14-card-sec14-F26.front: How often must Vermont vehicles pass inspection, and how soon after new registration without a valid sticker?
sec14-card-sec14-F26.expected_back: A vehicle must be inspected once a year and kept running properly at all times, a badly running vehicle can put you at fault in a crash, the sticker shows when the next inspection is due, and a newly registered vehicle must be inspected within fifteen days unless it already bears a valid Vermont sticker.

sec14-card-sec14-R05.front: How does Vermont's fifteen-day inspection rule pair with ongoing sticker renewals?
sec14-card-sec14-R05.expected_back: A newly registered vehicle must be inspected within fifteen days, while every vehicle is then inspected once a year as the sticker shows.

sec14-card-sec14-F27.front: How much fuel economy can cruising fifty-five or sixty instead of sixty-five on the interstate save?
sec14-card-sec14-F27.expected_back: Driving fifty-five or sixty miles per hour on the interstate instead of sixty-five saves fuel, and the Environmental Protection Agency estimates up to a fifteen percent improvement in fuel economy from that tip alone.

sec14-card-sec14-F28.front: How do jackrabbit starts, lane weaving, and hard braking hurt both fuel use and vehicle parts?
sec14-card-sec14-F28.expected_back: Accelerating smoothly from a stop and braking softly saves fuel, while fast starts, weaving and hard braking waste fuel and wear brakes and tires faster, so keep a safe distance and anticipate traffic to brake and accelerate gradually.

sec14-card-sec14-F29.front: How long should stationary winter warm-ups and in-town idling stay to protect lungs, engines, and fuel?
sec14-card-sec14-F29.expected_back: Idling wastes fuel, wears the engine and can cause respiratory illness, so clear snow and ice before starting, limit stationary warm ups to about thirty seconds when possible, and in town idling more than ten seconds uses more fuel than shutting off and restarting.

sec14-card-sec14-F30.front: What does Vermont's unattended motor-vehicle law require whenever you step away in public?
sec14-card-sec14-F30.expected_back: Leaving a vehicle idling unattended in public violates Vermont's unattended motor vehicle law, so if you leave the vehicle you must shut it off.

sec14-card-sec14-F31.front: Where is recommended tire pressure listed, and how much fuel can proper inflation save?
sec14-card-sec14-F31.expected_back: Keeping tires at the recommended pressure shown on the driver's door jamb placard and in the owner's manual can cut average fuel use by three to four percent, while under inflated tires raise rolling resistance, lower fuel economy and wear faster.

sec14-card-sec14-F32.front: Which upkeep items and cargo habits prevent making your engine burn extra fuel?
sec14-card-sec14-F32.expected_back: Keep the engine tuned, the wheels aligned and the air filters replaced as recommended, and carry no unnecessary weight such as trunk clutter or heavy roof luggage, because misaligned wheels and extra weight make the engine work harder and burn more fuel.

sec14-card-sec14-F33.front: How much fuel can trimming air-conditioner use above eighty degrees save, and what habits help?
sec14-card-sec14-F33.expected_back: Use heating and air conditioning selectively, since cutting air conditioner use when temperatures exceed eighty degrees can save ten to fifteen percent of fuel, prefer the vent setting and park in the shade.

sec14-card-sec14-F34.front: Above what speed should windows stay closed to prevent drag, and what trip habits cut fuel?
sec14-card-sec14-F34.expected_back: Drive with the windows closed unless your speed stays under fifty miles per hour, because open windows at highway speed add aerodynamic drag and lower fuel economy, and consolidate trips and car pool to save miles and fuel.

sec06-card-sec06-F01.front: What does a railroad crossbuck sign mark, and what three actions should you take before crossing?
sec06-card-sec06-F01.expected_back: Crossbuck signs stand at every railroad crossing to show where the tracks are, and a driver should slow down, look both ways and listen for trains before crossing.

sec06-card-sec06-F02.front: What does the small plaque below a crossbuck show, and what hidden danger comes with multiple tracks?
sec06-card-sec06-F02.expected_back: A smaller sign below the crossbuck tells how many tracks the crossing has, and where there are two or more tracks one passing train can hide a second train coming the other way; gates and flashing lights may also be present.

sec06-card-sec06-F03.front: Where will you see a triangle sign with its three points cut off, and what does it mean?
sec06-card-sec06-F03.expected_back: A triangle shaped sign with its points cut off is displayed on vehicles that travel at slow speeds, such as farm vehicles.

sec06-card-sec06-F04.front: What shape and colors identify standard warning signs, and what driver action do they call for?
sec06-card-sec06-F04.expected_back: Warning signs are placed where danger exists at all times and tell a driver to slow down; they are usually diamond shaped and yellow or green and may warn of sharp curves, unsafe intersections or dips in the road.

sec06-card-sec06-R01.front: How do you tell a roadside warning sign apart from a slow-moving farm emblem by shape?
sec06-card-sec06-R01.expected_back: Warning signs are usually diamond-shaped and yellow or green, whereas a triangle sign with cut-off points is displayed on slow-moving vehicles such as farm vehicles.

sec06-card-sec06-F05.front: What extra details can accompany a warning sign, and what does a downward arrow under a pedestrian or school sign mark?
sec06-card-sec06-F05.expected_back: Some warning signs add information such as a safe speed or a distance, and a downward arrow under a school or pedestrian sign marks a crosswalk or crossing area.

sec06-card-sec06-F06.front: What shape and background color mark regulatory signs, and what kind of message do they give?
sec06-card-sec06-F06.expected_back: Regulatory signs are rectangular with white backgrounds and state what a driver must or must not do, including speed limits, turning and passing laws and other directions.

sec06-card-sec06-R02.front: When snow or dirt hides a sign's lettering, how does shape separate regulatory rules from hazard warnings?
sec06-card-sec06-R02.expected_back: A regulatory sign is a white rectangle that states a rule, whereas a warning sign is usually a yellow or green diamond that flags a danger, and the shape alone tells them apart when the face is obscured.

sec06-card-sec06-F23.front: Which color and two shapes identify work-zone signs, and what hazards do they announce?
sec06-card-sec06-F23.expected_back: Work zone signs are orange and shaped as diamonds or rectangles, and they warn of hazards ahead such as closed lanes, detours, rough pavement or flaggers.

sec06-card-sec06-R06.front: Alongside orange diamond or rectangular work signs, what legal status does a work-zone flagger hold?
sec06-card-sec06-R06.expected_back: Work zone signs are orange and diamond- or rectangular-shaped to warn of hazards ahead, and a flagger has legal authority to control traffic and must be obeyed.

sec06-card-sec06-F07.front: What four jobs do highway pavement markings perform, and what color are center lines on major highways?
sec06-card-sec06-F07.expected_back: Highway markings help a driver position the vehicle, direct the driver through situations, show when passing is allowed and warn of conditions ahead, and major highways carry yellow center lines.

sec06-card-sec06-F08.front: On an undivided multilane road, what separates opposing directions versus lanes moving the same way?
sec06-card-sec06-F08.expected_back: Center lines divide a highway into travel lanes, a multilane highway without a median uses double solid lines to separate the two opposing directions, and a broken white line divides lanes carrying traffic in the same direction.

sec06-card-sec06-R04.front: How do double solid yellow lines contrast with broken white lines on an undivided multilane highway?
sec06-card-sec06-R04.expected_back: Double solid yellow lines separate opposing directions on an undivided multilane highway, while broken white lines separate lanes moving the same way.

sec06-card-sec06-F09.front: How do single solid, double solid, and paired broken-and-solid center lines control passing?
sec06-card-sec06-F09.expected_back: Where there is a solid line or two solid lines it is recommended not to pass, where a broken line is on your side next to a solid line you may pass when the road ahead is clear, and where the solid line is on your side and the broken line on the other you should not pass while the other lane's traffic may.

sec06-card-sec06-R03.front: When one center stripe is solid and the other is broken, which stripe governs your lane?
sec06-card-sec06-R03.expected_back: Passing is judged by the line nearest your lane: a broken line on your side allows a pass when clear, while a solid line on your side forbids it even if the far side is broken.

sec06-card-sec06-F27.front: In a work zone with temporary markers, which color belongs on your left, and what if it is not?
sec06-card-sec06-F27.expected_back: Work zones may use temporary pavement markings where white markers or lines separate lanes going the same way and yellow markers or lines separate opposing lanes, so yellow markings should be on your left and if they are not you are in the wrong lane.

sec06-card-sec06-F10.front: How must you enter and use a continuous two-way left-turn lane, and what is it never used for?
sec06-card-sec06-F10.expected_back: A continuous two way left turn lane is not a travel lane, because traffic in both directions may use it to turn left; a short distance before the turn signal, move the whole vehicle into the lane so traffic is not blocked, and turn when the way is clear.

sec06-card-sec06-F11.front: What does a painted row of white triangles pointing toward approaching vehicles mark at an intersection?
sec06-card-sec06-F11.expected_back: At a yield intersection a yield line, a row of white triangles pointing toward approaching cars, may be painted on the road to show where drivers should stop when they must yield to pedestrians or other vehicles.

sec06-card-sec06-F12.front: When turning onto a multilane road, which lane must a right-turning driver and a left-turning driver each enter first?
sec06-card-sec06-F12.expected_back: When turning from one road onto a multilane road with a choice of lanes, a right turning driver must turn into the right lane and a left turning driver must first turn into the left lane.

sec06-card-sec06-F13.front: When are multiple lanes allowed to turn together, and how must each driver track through the turn?
sec06-card-sec06-F13.expected_back: Where two lanes turn in the same direction each turning lane must keep to its own path throughout the turn, multiple lanes may turn together only when lane use signs or pavement markings allow it, and a driver stays in the designated lane until the turn is complete.

sec06-card-sec06-F14.front: Why must you finish a turn completely before changing lanes?
sec06-card-sec06-F14.expected_back: Lane changes belong after a turn is finished, because changing lanes while turning is an illegal maneuver that leads to crashes.

sec06-card-sec06-R05.front: What separates a legal post-turn lane change from an illegal turn maneuver?
sec06-card-sec06-R05.expected_back: A lane change after completing a turn is normal driving, while a lane change during the turn is an illegal maneuver.

sec06-card-sec06-F15.front: If you realize too late that you are in a straight-arrow lane when you wanted to turn, what should you do?
sec06-card-sec06-F15.expected_back: A driver must follow through on the direction marked in the lane, so a driver in a straight arrow lane may not legally turn right or left at the intersection, and it is safer to drive around the block than to make a sudden lane change.

sec06-card-sec06-F16.front: What activities count as a highway work zone, including slow-moving mobile operations?
sec06-card-sec06-F16.expected_back: A work zone is a highway area with construction, maintenance or utility work, and it may be stationary or a mobile operation moving slowly down the road, such as line striping, mowing or snow removal.

sec06-card-sec06-F17.front: Where do many work-zone collisions actually occur, and what crash type is most common?
sec06-card-sec06-F17.expected_back: Many work zone crashes happen before the actual work area where drivers slow and merge, so drivers should merge into the correct lane as soon as it is safe, and most work zone crashes are rear end crashes from driving too fast for conditions and following too closely, with stopped traffic possibly hidden around a curve or over a hill.

sec06-card-sec06-F18.front: Do work-zone speed and safety rules stop overnight, and how should you adjust speed in bad weather?
sec06-card-sec06-F18.expected_back: Work zone rules apply around the clock, not just in daylight, and drivers should slow to the posted limit and adjust further for weather, because speeds are lowered to protect both motorists and workers.

sec06-card-sec06-F19.front: What focus and lane discipline does the Vermont manual expect from drivers inside a work zone?
sec06-card-sec06-F19.expected_back: In a work zone give the road full attention, expect pedestrians, bicyclists and every other mode of travel, follow the signs, and avoid changing lanes, tailgating or other aggressive behavior.

sec06-card-sec06-F20.front: What following gap and merging habits protect crews and traffic through a work zone?
sec06-card-sec06-F20.expected_back: Work zone drivers should merge as instructed as soon as it is safe, leave workers and equipment as much space as possible, keep a four second following distance, and be patient about delays or take another route.

sec06-card-sec06-F21.front: On dry pavement, how many feet does a passenger car need to stop from sixty miles per hour versus thirty?
sec06-card-sec06-F21.expected_back: On dry pavement a passenger car traveling at sixty miles per hour needs two hundred forty feet to come to a complete stop, compared with seventy-five feet for the same car at thirty miles per hour.

sec06-card-sec06-F22.front: What happens to the fine penalty if you are caught speeding in a Vermont work zone?
sec06-card-sec06-F22.expected_back: Fines are doubled for speeding in a work zone.

sec06-card-sec06-F24.front: Why does work-zone traffic often stop completely, and what tools and authority do flaggers use?
sec06-card-sec06-F24.expected_back: Traffic often must stop in a work zone so equipment can move or because only one lane is open for both directions, flaggers guide traffic with stop and slow paddles or sometimes orange flags, and a flagger has legal authority to control traffic and must be obeyed.

sec06-card-sec06-F25.front: What role do cones, drums, and barricades serve as channeling devices in a work zone?
sec06-card-sec06-F25.expected_back: Cones, drums and barricades are channeling devices used to keep traffic out of hazardous roadwork areas and to guide it safely through the work zone.

sec06-card-sec06-F26.front: Besides directional merge arrows, what does caution mode look like on a flashing work-zone panel, and what does it mean?
sec06-card-sec06-F26.expected_back: Flashing arrow panels guide drivers into the correct lane, and when no arrow is needed the panel shows caution mode, a straight line of blinking lights or blinking lights on its four corners, which tells drivers to slow down.

sec09-card-sec09-F21.front: What driver mistake causes most skids on slick surfaces, and which convenience feature must stay off?
sec09-card-sec09-F21.expected_back: Most skids come from a driver failing to adjust speed in time to road and traffic conditions such as snow, ice, rain, dirt, gravel and wet leaves, and cruise control must not be used in those conditions.

sec09-card-sec09-F22.front: How does skid warning differ between rear-wheel and front-wheel drive, and what snow trap catches front-wheel drivers?
sec09-card-sec09-F22.expected_back: A rear wheel drive vehicle usually gives a feel of lost traction before a skid, but a front wheel drive may give no warning, and although front wheel drive handles better in snow its traction is not flawless, so its better feel must not tempt you to drive faster.

sec09-card-sec09-F23.front: With standard non-ABS brakes, how should you shed speed on a slippery road without locking the wheels?
sec09-card-sec09-F23.expected_back: On a possibly slippery road drive slower, avoid sudden changes of speed or direction, slow by lifting off the gas, and if more slowing is needed squeeze the brakes with slow steady pressure, keep the wheels rolling, ease off if they begin to lock, and consider shifting to a lower gear.

sec09-card-sec09-R01.front: On slick pavement, how does proper pedal work differ between ordinary brakes and anti-lock brakes?
sec09-card-sec09-R01.expected_back: With ordinary brakes on a slippery road you squeeze gently and ease off if the wheels lock, but with anti-lock brakes you hold steady pressure and never pump.

sec09-card-sec09-R02.front: How does brake use change once you switch from preventing a skid to recovering from an active skid?
sec09-card-sec09-R02.expected_back: Skid prevention relies on gentle speed reduction, while skid recovery forbids braking altogether and depends on steering toward the intended path.

sec09-card-sec09-F24.front: How should you press the brake pedal in an anti-lock-equipped car, and what old habit must you avoid?
sec09-card-sec09-F24.expected_back: With anti-lock brakes use steady brake pressure and do not pump the brakes, following the owner's manual.

sec09-card-sec09-F25.front: Whether driving front- or rear-wheel drive, what exact steps bring a skidding vehicle back under control?
sec09-card-sec09-F25.expected_back: Skid recovery is the same for front and rear wheel drive: do not hit the brakes, which worsens the skid, steer in the direction you want the vehicle to go, and expect to steer left and right a few times before full control returns.

sec09-card-sec09-F26.front: Do stability systems or all-wheel drive help you grip glare ice, and where should you test winter handling?
sec09-card-sec09-F26.expected_back: Stability control and similar improvements can help but never substitute for driver caution, four wheel and all wheel drive have better traction in snow but not on ice, and every driver should learn how the vehicle handles on ice or snow in an empty parking lot.

sec09-card-sec09-F27.front: What crucial maneuver do anti-lock brakes allow, and what normal pedal sensations happen when they activate?
sec09-card-sec09-F27.expected_back: Anti-lock brakes let you brake and steer at the same time, and noise and vibration in the pedal are normal when they engage.

sec09-card-sec09-F28.front: What foot mistake turns anti-lock protection off mid-stop, and how do you confirm your car has ABS?
sec09-card-sec09-F28.expected_back: Pumping the brake or lifting your foot off the pedal disengages the anti-lock system, the owner's manual tells you whether the vehicle has it, and the anti-lock warning light shows briefly at start up.

sec09-card-sec09-R03.front: How do you interpret an anti-lock dash light that blinks briefly at startup versus one staying lit on the road?
sec09-card-sec09-R03.expected_back: A brief anti-lock light at start up is normal, while a light that stays lit while driving means the anti-lock function is lost even though normal braking remains.

sec09-card-sec09-F29.front: If your anti-lock brake warning light stays illuminated while driving, do you still have working brakes?
sec09-card-sec09-F29.expected_back: If the anti-lock warning light stays on after you begin driving, the anti-lock system is not working, although the vehicle still has ordinary brakes.

sec09-card-sec09-F08.front: Which headlight beam belongs in fog or heavy snow, and at what visibility distance does Vermont require headlights?
sec09-card-sec09-F08.expected_back: In fog, heavy rain or heavy snow use low beam headlights, and the law requires headlights on whenever you cannot clearly see persons or vehicles five hundred feet ahead.

sec09-card-sec09-F30.front: By how much do daytime low-beam headlights cut head-on crash risk, and what trap comes with daytime running lights?
sec09-card-sec09-F30.expected_back: Studies show that driving with low beam headlights on in daytime reduces the risk of head on collisions by more than twenty percent, and daytime running lights that come on automatically must not be mistaken for headlights.

sec09-card-sec09-F31.front: When weather limits sight, what lights are required, and when are parking lights legal to use?
sec09-card-sec09-F31.expected_back: When snow, rain or fog limit visibility you must turn the headlights on, the best practice is to drive with at least low beams on even by day, and parking lights are only for a parked vehicle.

sec09-card-sec09-F32.front: During which exact night hours does Vermont law require headlights, and why switch them on manually?
sec09-card-sec09-F32.expected_back: Night driving is more dangerous because you cannot see as far ahead, and the law requires headlights on from a half hour after sunset until a half hour before sunrise, so switch them on yourself because daytime running lights can make you think they already are.

sec09-card-sec09-R04.front: What two independent legal triggers, one by clock and one by sight distance, require headlights in Vermont?
sec09-card-sec09-R04.expected_back: The clock rule puts headlights on from a half hour after sunset to a half hour before sunrise, while the visibility rule requires them any time persons or vehicles cannot be seen five hundred feet ahead.

sec09-card-sec09-F33.front: What sight cushion do you always need ahead, and at what night speed are you already overdriving low beams?
sec09-card-sec09-F33.expected_back: You always need to see four seconds ahead, and at night at forty miles per hour on low beams you are overdriving your headlights, unable to stop within the distance you can see.

sec09-card-sec09-F34.front: Where do high beams belong at night, and which four situations require switching to low beams?
sec09-card-sec09-F34.expected_back: Use high beams in open country with few other vehicles, keeping speed lower than by day even with them, and use low beams when approaching other vehicles or pedestrians, in areas with streetlights or fog, and when following another vehicle.

sec09-card-sec09-R05.front: How do high beams, low beams, and daytime running lights divide up open country, traffic or fog, and full headlights?
sec09-card-sec09-R05.expected_back: High beams belong on open country roads with few vehicles, while low beams are required when meeting, following, under streetlights or in fog, and daytime running lights are neither.

sec09-card-sec09-F35.front: When should you dim high beams for others, and where should you aim your eyes if oncoming lights blind you?
sec09-card-sec09-F35.expected_back: A courteous night driver promptly dims the headlights when meeting or following another vehicle, and to avoid being blinded by oncoming lights looks ahead toward the right edge of the road rather than directly at them.

sec09-card-sec09-F01.front: How deadly are flash floods nationwide for motorists, and what is the smartest call when severe weather is forecast?
sec09-card-sec09-F01.expected_back: Nationally, flash floods kill more people than any other weather event and nearly half of those deaths are vehicle related, so when hazardous driving conditions are forecast the best choice is to stay home and avoid unnecessary travel.

sec09-card-sec09-F02.front: What speed, cruise-control, and following-gap adjustments apply if a storm hits while you are driving?
sec09-card-sec09-F02.expected_back: If a storm catches you on the road, slow down, switch cruise control off, stay alert, leave a gap of more than four seconds to the vehicle ahead, and take extra care at night or on roads you do not know.

sec09-card-sec09-F03.front: Why must you obey detour signs and never drive past road-closed signs or around flood barricades?
sec09-card-sec09-F03.expected_back: Flood waters may wash away or undermine bridges, culverts and roadbeds, so never drive around traffic barricades or past road closed signs, and obey every detour sign.

sec09-card-sec09-F04.front: What three dangers make driving across water-covered pavement a trap?
sec09-card-sec09-F04.expected_back: Do not drive where water covers the road, because its depth is not obvious, it can hide washouts, and a vehicle's motor will stall in water, leaving you stranded or trapped.

sec09-card-sec09-F05.front: What must you do immediately if your car stalls in floodwater, and how shallow can dangerous moving water be?
sec09-card-sec09-F05.expected_back: Should your car stall in floodwater, leave it right away: rising water can sweep away a vehicle and its occupants, many fatalities happen while trying to move stalled cars, and even four inches of moving water impairs walking and conceals hazards.

sec09-card-sec09-F06.front: Which vehicles feel strong crosswinds worst, and how must you treat storm-downed trees and utility wires?
sec09-card-sec09-F06.expected_back: Wind endangers all motorists but especially large vehicles and drivers towing trailers, so slower speeds are the best practice, and strong wind, heavy snow or ice can drop trees and wires into the road, which you must never approach or cross.

sec09-card-sec09-F07.front: Which official alerts should every driver check before heading out in questionable weather?
sec09-card-sec09-F07.expected_back: Check Weather Service flash flood and weather warnings and all hazardous driving notices before traveling.

sec09-card-sec09-F09.front: Which vehicle systems and two cold-weather fluids must be ready before Vermont winter arrives?
sec09-card-sec09-F09.expected_back: Winter is the hardest driving season because of snow, ice and fewer daylight hours, so brakes, wipers, defroster, heater and exhaust must be in top condition, antifreeze checked, and the washer reservoir filled with a winter fluid.

sec09-card-sec09-F10.front: How many wheels need snow tires before the first snowfall, and what tire-mixing mistake must you avoid?
sec09-card-sec09-F10.expected_back: Put good snow tires on all four wheels early so the first snowfall does not catch you without them, and never combine different types of tires on the same vehicle.

sec09-card-sec09-F12.front: If you must drive during a winter storm, how thoroughly must you clear the car, wipers, and glass?
sec09-card-sec09-F12.expected_back: During ice or snow storms, especially under a traveler's advisory, do not drive unless absolutely necessary, and if you must, clear all ice and snow from the entire vehicle, keep the wipers free of ice and the inside of the windows free of moisture.

sec09-card-sec09-F13.front: Which three elevated road structures freeze before regular pavement when sleet or freezing rain starts?
sec09-card-sec09-F13.expected_back: When sleet, freezing rain or snow begins, black ice can form quickly and invisibly, bridges, ramps and overpasses freeze first, and slippery spots can remain after plows clear the highway.

sec09-card-sec09-F14.front: How much following gap do winter roads demand, and why can't four-wheel drive shorten your braking?
sec09-card-sec09-F14.expected_back: On winter roads allow extra travel time, increase following distance to more than four seconds, and remember that even four wheel or all wheel drive vehicles lack good traction on ice and every vehicle struggles to stop, curve and change lanes.

sec09-card-sec09-R06.front: Why must four-wheel and all-wheel-drive drivers still stretch winter following distances past four seconds?
sec09-card-sec09-R06.expected_back: Four wheel and all wheel drive give better traction in snow but no advantage on ice, which is why the winter following distance rises above four seconds for every vehicle.

sec09-card-sec09-F16.front: What survival gear belongs in a Vermont winter car kit, and what minimum fuel reading should you keep?
sec09-card-sec09-F16.expected_back: A winter vehicle kit should hold a windshield scraper and brush, a small shovel, kitty litter or sand, extra clothing, food and water, a cell phone, extra washer fluid, a basic first aid kit and a flashlight, and the gas tank should always be at least half full.

sec09-card-sec09-F11.front: When do many states permit metal-studded tires, and what tire maintenance rule applies year-round?
sec09-card-sec09-F11.expected_back: Many states allow metal studded tires only in winter conditions, and tires must always be properly inflated.

sec09-card-sec09-F15.front: What three traits make snowplows tricky to share the road with, and how should winter trips be planned?
sec09-card-sec09-F15.expected_back: Be especially careful near snowplows, which are hard to see in the snow cloud they create, are wider than other vehicles and often move slowly, and in winter travel by day, not alone, on main roads, with others informed of your route and schedule.

sec09-card-sec09-F17.front: If a blizzard strands you, how should you mark the car, and why stay inside instead of walking?
