sec07-card-sec07-F12.teaching_text: Playing kids dart without looking and older pedestrians may not hear or sense a car emerging from a driveway.

sec07-card-sec07-F13.question_text: Is it permissible to stop and pick up hitchhikers along an interstate highway or its ramps?
sec07-card-sec07-F13.teaching_text: Stopping along high-speed interstate lanes or ramps to pick up hitchhikers invites catastrophic rear-end collisions.

sec07-card-sec07-F14.question_text: What exact action must you take when a pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog is crossing or waiting to cross?
sec07-card-sec07-F14.teaching_text: Blind or visually impaired walkers rely on traffic coming to a complete stop rather than rolling past them.

sec07-card-sec07-R04.question_text: How does your legal duty toward someone using a white cane or guide dog exceed ordinary pedestrian yielding?
sec07-card-sec07-R04.teaching_text: While ordinary yielding may only require slowing enough to let walkers pass, white canes and guide dogs mandate stopping.

sec07-card-sec07-F15.question_text: What pedestrian and signal rules govern turning at intersections, especially when facing a red arrow?
sec07-card-sec07-F15.teaching_text: Watch lighted no-turn-on-red warnings during walk phases, and treat every red arrow as an absolute turn ban.

sec07-card-sec07-F16.question_text: What does a pedestrian sign placed right in the roadway at a marked crosswalk remind drivers to do?
sec07-card-sec07-F16.teaching_text: Centerline crosswalk paddles reinforce that motorists must yield whenever walkers occupy the marked crossing.

sec07-card-sec07-F30.question_text: Which Vermont roads may bicyclists legally use, and which traffic rules apply to them?
sec07-card-sec07-F30.teaching_text: Outside limited-access interstates and posted bans, cyclists ride under the exact same traffic laws as motorists.

sec07-card-sec07-F31.question_text: How should you approach and pass a bicycle, and why shouldn't you honk without good reason?
sec07-card-sec07-F31.teaching_text: An unexpected horn blast right behind a quiet bicycle can startle the rider into wobbling straight into your car.

sec07-card-sec07-F32.question_text: Why is a bicyclist legally allowed to ride toward the center of a lane instead of hugging the edge?
sec07-card-sec07-F32.teaching_text: Unseen edge debris, glass, or upcoming turn lanes give cyclists the legal right to claim center-lane space.

sec07-card-sec07-F35.question_text: What minimum side gap must you leave when passing a bicyclist, and what if the road is too narrow?
sec07-card-sec07-F35.teaching_text: Squeezing past closer than four feet risks mirror strikes and wind buffeting, so hold back on narrow lanes.

sec07-card-sec07-R05.question_text: How does your four-foot passing duty interact with a bicyclist's right to occupy a narrow lane?
sec07-card-sec07-R05.teaching_text: When a lane cannot fit your car plus four feet of clearance, the cyclist keeps the lane until passing widens.

sec07-card-sec07-F36.question_text: Is it legal for two bicyclists to ride side by side, and how should an approaching driver respond?
sec07-card-sec07-F36.teaching_text: Two-abreast riding is lawful, so ease off the gas and pass only when sightlines and clearance are safe.

sec07-card-sec07-F37.question_text: How must a left-turning driver treat an oncoming bicyclist, and what speed illusion catches drivers off guard?
sec07-card-sec07-F37.teaching_text: Drivers misjudge slim bicycles as slow and turn left right across a rider moving faster than expected.

sec07-card-sec07-F38.question_text: What four everyday driver mistakes most commonly strike bicyclists?
sec07-card-sec07-F38.teaching_text: Checking mirrors, blind spots, and curb lanes before turning, pulling out, or swinging doors prevents most bike collisions.

sec07-card-sec07-F17.question_text: What three things must you stay alert for whenever signs or flashing lights mark a school zone?
sec07-card-sec07-F17.teaching_text: School approaches mix unpredictable young walkers with buses pulling in and out of traffic.

sec07-card-sec07-F18.question_text: When do reduced school-zone speed limits apply, and why must you still watch outside weekday class hours?
sec07-card-sec07-F18.teaching_text: Playgrounds and ballfields draw children after class and all weekend, not just during morning and afternoon bells.

sec07-card-sec07-F19.question_text: Why must you take extra care in residential neighborhoods, especially when backing in or out of a driveway?
sec07-card-sec07-F19.teaching_text: Small children playing near garages sit below rear window sightlines and can dart behind reversing tires.

sec07-card-sec07-F20.question_text: What legal duty stops a pedestrian from stepping off a curb straight in front of a close vehicle?
sec07-card-sec07-F20.teaching_text: Physics prevents heavy cars from stopping instantly, so walkers may not dart abruptly into unavoidable range.

sec07-card-sec07-F21.question_text: How should a pedestrian respond to a flashing Don't Walk signal if still on the curb versus already crossing?
sec07-card-sec07-F21.teaching_text: The flashing phase clears walkers already in the street while barring anyone new from leaving the curb.

sec07-card-sec07-F22.question_text: Where no pedestrian signals exist, on which traffic light should a walker cross, and what danger remains?
sec07-card-sec07-F22.teaching_text: Walking parallel to green traffic aligns your crossing phase, though right- and left-turning cars can still swing across.

sec07-card-sec07-F23.question_text: When a road has no sidewalk, which side and direction must a pedestrian use?
sec07-card-sec07-F23.teaching_text: Facing oncoming headlights lets you see approaching cars and step clear instead of having traffic sneak up behind.

sec07-card-sec07-R06.question_text: On a road without sidewalks, how does a pedestrian's road side compare with a bicyclist's?
sec07-card-sec07-R06.teaching_text: Exam questions flip these constantly because pedestrians walk left facing cars while bicycles ride right with traffic.

sec07-card-sec07-F24.question_text: What clothing, light, and headphone habits keep pedestrians safer, especially from dusk through dawn?
sec07-card-sec07-F24.teaching_text: Bright or reflective clothes plus a light help drivers spot you, and skipping headphones keeps traffic audible.

sec07-card-sec07-F39.question_text: Do bicyclists need a license, when may they ride two abreast, and can they receive traffic tickets?
sec07-card-sec07-F39.teaching_text: Riders need no license and may pair up if traffic flows freely, yet traffic violations still bring fines.

sec07-card-sec07-F40.question_text: How should a bicyclist ride past parked cars, handle right-turn lanes when going straight, and signal turns?
sec07-card-sec07-F40.teaching_text: Holding a steady line outside right-turn-only lanes and signaling by hand lets surrounding drivers predict every move.

sec10-card-sec10-F08.question_text: How should you use your eyes, mirrors, and following count on a Vermont interstate?
sec10-card-sec10-F08.teaching_text: Active mirror checks plus four seconds of dry buffer or more on wet asphalt prevent pileups.

sec10-card-sec10-F09.question_text: How should you communicate and check before changing lanes or passing on the interstate?
sec10-card-sec10-F09.teaching_text: Abrupt braking or constant lane hopping surprises seventy-mile-per-hour traffic around your blind spots.

sec10-card-sec10-F10.question_text: When is stopping legal on an interstate, and how do you position and signal for help?
sec10-card-sec10-F10.teaching_text: Pulling far right into the breakdown lane with raised hood, white cloth, and occupants inside protects lives.

sec10-card-sec10-F11.question_text: Which lane should you normally travel in on a Vermont interstate?
sec10-card-sec10-F11.teaching_text: Cruising right keeps the left lane clear for overtaking traffic unless overhead signs direct otherwise.

sec10-card-sec10-F12.question_text: Why must you avoid driving tired on the interstate, and what should you do if drowsiness hits?
sec10-card-sec10-F12.teaching_text: Fatigue ranks among major interstate crash causes, making a prompt safe rest stop essential.

sec10-card-sec10-F14.question_text: What must you do after missing an interstate exit, and which two shortcuts are illegal?
sec10-card-sec10-F14.teaching_text: Backing up or cutting across emergency turnarounds puts slow cars straight into high-speed lanes.

sec10-card-sec10-R03.question_text: Which one lawful option replaces backing up or using a median crossover after missing an exit?
sec10-card-sec10-R03.teaching_text: Emergency crossovers belong strictly to patrol and maintenance crews, never drivers who missed ramps.

sec10-card-sec10-F15.question_text: In which four weather or surface conditions must you never engage cruise control?
sec10-card-sec10-F15.teaching_text: Cruise control keeps spinning lost-grip tires on slick patches instead of letting speed ease smoothly.
sec10-card-sec10-F15.must_match_memory_hook: Never use rain, fog, snow, ice

visual_sync.text_span: Never use rain, fog, snow, ice

sec10-card-sec10-F16.question_text: How must you pass a stopped police, emergency, or repair vehicle displaying flashing lights?
sec10-card-sec10-F16.teaching_text: Shifting one lane away protects roadside workers, with twenty below the limit required when boxed in.

sec10-card-sec10-R02.question_text: When does Vermont's twenty-mile-per-hour-under rule apply past a stopped emergency vehicle instead of changing lanes?
sec10-card-sec10-R02.teaching_text: Moving over a full lane comes first whenever safe, leaving twenty-under strictly as the fallback.

sec10-card-sec10-F18.question_text: What sequence of checks and signals comes before pulling left to pass a vehicle or bicycle?
sec10-card-sec10-F18.teaching_text: Glancing over your left shoulder confirms nobody is already overtaking your car from behind.

sec10-card-sec10-F22.question_text: What side clearance is required when overtaking on the left, and when may you merge back right?
sec10-card-sec10-F22.teaching_text: Giving four feet and waiting until the full front or cyclist appears inside your rearview prevents cutoffs.

sec10-card-sec10-F23.question_text: What two courteous adjustments should you make while another driver passes you?
sec10-card-sec10-F23.teaching_text: Dropping a touch of speed while hugging right shortens the passer's exposure significantly.

sec10-card-sec10-F24.question_text: In which two roadway situations may a Vermont driver pass on the right?
sec10-card-sec10-F24.teaching_text: Right-side overtaking works on multilane roads or safely past a car or bike turning left.

sec10-card-sec10-R04.question_text: What strict surface boundary separates a legal right-side pass from an illegal one?
sec10-card-sec10-R04.teaching_text: Even around a left-turning car, dropping tires onto gravel or shoulders makes passing illegal.

sec10-card-sec10-F25.question_text: Under what circumstances may you drive off the pavement or main traveled road to pass?
sec10-card-sec10-F25.teaching_text: Shoulders carry soft edges, guardrails, cyclists, and parked breakdowns with zero passing allowance.

sec10-card-sec10-F26.question_text: At which five road features or sign zones is passing strictly prohibited?
sec10-card-sec10-F26.teaching_text: Blind geometry and changed-path-ahead zones hide oncoming traffic and shifting lane widths.

sec10-card-sec10-F02.question_text: How are interstates built, and what six other names do regions use for free or tolled highways?
sec10-card-sec10-F02.teaching_text: Whether called throughways, turnpikes, toll roads, or freeways, all share divided high-speed design.

sec10-card-sec10-F03.question_text: What travel benefit comes from an interstate's multi-lane, controlled-access layout?
sec10-card-sec10-F03.teaching_text: Eliminating cross-street lights and driveways makes long-distance travel smoother when drivers merge properly.

sec10-card-sec10-F04.question_text: Where do speed-change lanes run, and how do they connect ramps with interstate travel lanes?
sec10-card-sec10-F04.teaching_text: Dedicated side lanes let entering cars match pace and exiting cars shed speed off-mainline.

sec10-card-sec10-F05.question_text: What five-step sequence takes you smoothly from an entrance ramp onto the interstate?
sec10-card-sec10-F05.teaching_text: Reaching interstate speed and checking your left shoulder before merging prevents cutting off mainline cars.
sec10-card-sec10-F05.must_match_memory_hook: Stay right, signal, accelerate, check, merge

visual_sync.text_span: Stay right, signal, accelerate, check, merge

sec10-card-sec10-R01.question_text: How does speed timing differ between an interstate entrance ramp and an exit ramp?
sec10-card-sec10-R01.teaching_text: Mergers build speed while yielding, whereas exiters hold highway speed until inside the deceleration lane.

sec10-card-sec10-F06.question_text: Who must yield when a vehicle enters the interstate from a ramp?
sec10-card-sec10-F06.teaching_text: Through traffic already cruising on the interstate holds right-of-way over merging ramp cars.

sec10-card-sec10-F07.question_text: What three steps take you cleanly off the interstate onto an exit ramp?
sec10-card-sec10-F07.teaching_text: Signaling into the nearest deceleration lane before slowing protects fast cars behind you.

sec10-card-sec10-F01.question_text: Where should you aim your eyes against bright oncoming headlights, and what bonus hazard does it spot?
sec10-card-sec10-F01.teaching_text: Tracking the white right edge protects night vision while catching cyclists or pedestrians along the shoulder.

sec10-card-sec10-F13.question_text: Why do snowy or icy interstates, ramps, bridges, and overpasses demand extra speed reductions?
sec10-card-sec10-F13.teaching_text: Exposed bridge and overpass decks ice up faster and stay slicker than insulated main pavement.

sec10-card-sec10-F17.question_text: What does seeing a yellow edge line on your right side along a divided highway mean?
sec10-card-sec10-F17.teaching_text: Divided highways keep yellow on the median left and white on the right shoulder.

sec10-card-sec10-R05.question_text: Which edge-line color belongs on your right on an interstate, and what warns you of wrong-way travel?
sec10-card-sec10-R05.teaching_text: Spotting yellow paint along your right passenger window demands immediate safe corrective action.

sec10-card-sec10-F19.question_text: How can you alert a driver ahead of your intention to pass at night?
sec10-card-sec10-F19.teaching_text: A brief low-high-low beam pulse catches the lead driver's mirrors before you pull alongside.

sec10-card-sec10-F20.question_text: What extra precaution is vital before returning right after passing while towing a trailer?
sec10-card-sec10-F20.teaching_text: Returning at normal car distance swings your trailing hitch and cargo straight into the passed vehicle.

sec10-card-sec10-F21.question_text: When must you take extra side-clearance care around motorists and bicyclists while passing?
sec10-card-sec10-F21.teaching_text: Extended mirrors, campers, or wide trailers shrink lateral margin far tighter than a standard car.

sec08-card-sec08-F13.question_text: How should you think of a moving motorcycle, and which manual covers motorcycle permits and endorsements?
sec08-card-sec08-F13.teaching_text: Viewing an exposed rider as a human being builds caution, while the Vermont Motorcycle Manual covers licensing rules.

sec08-card-sec08-F14.question_text: In over seventy percent of fatal car-truck crashes, which driver caused the wreck, and in what weather?
sec08-card-sec08-F14.teaching_text: Over two hundred fifty thousand car-truck collisions happen yearly, mostly in good daylight weather from car-driver mistakes.

sec08-card-sec08-F15.question_text: In four out of every five fatal collisions involving a large truck, who is the person killed?
sec08-card-sec08-F15.teaching_text: Massive weight differences mean passenger-vehicle drivers suffer most fatalities when motorists misjudge truck stopping and turning limits.

sec08-card-sec08-F16.question_text: Which four driving demands expand as a truck gets larger?
sec08-card-sec08-F16.teaching_text: Longer, heavier rigs hide bigger zones, swing wider, brake farther, and require more road ahead to overtake.

sec08-card-sec08-F17.question_text: Where sit a large truck's no-zones, and what simple mirror check tells you whether the driver can see you?
sec08-card-sec08-F17.teaching_text: Front, rear, and side blind zones swallow cars whole whenever you cannot see the rig's side mirrors.

sec08-card-sec08-F18.question_text: When overtaking a large truck, what must appear in your inside rearview mirror before you merge back right?
sec08-card-sec08-F18.teaching_text: Cutting back before the entire tractor cab shows in your rearview mirror steals the rig's heavy braking cushion.

sec08-card-sec08-F19.question_text: Why must you wait patiently instead of driving around a truck that is backing or setting up to back?
sec08-card-sec08-F19.teaching_text: Long trailers block sightlines completely, so squeezing past puts your car straight into an active blind spot.

sec08-card-sec08-F20.question_text: What two visibility losses make following closely right behind a large truck so hazardous?
sec08-card-sec08-F20.teaching_text: Riding a trailer bumper hides you from the trucker's mirrors while blocking your own sight of sudden braking ahead.

sec08-card-sec08-R03.question_text: How does the crash risk in a truck's rear no-zone differ from lingering in its side no-zones?
sec08-card-sec08-R03.teaching_text: Tailgating invites rear-end underride crashes, while cruising beside a trailer risks getting crushed during a lane change.

sec08-card-sec08-F21.question_text: Why is lingering alongside either side of a large truck far riskier than driving beside a passenger car?
sec08-card-sec08-F21.teaching_text: Trailers cast massive blind zones down both flanks where an unseen car gets swept by a lane shift.

sec08-card-sec08-F22.question_text: Why do trucks often swing left before turning right, and what curb mistake must drivers never make?
sec08-card-sec08-F22.teaching_text: Sneaking between a right-signaling trailer and the curb traps your car inside the trailer's off-tracking path.

sec08-card-sec08-F02.question_text: How do a motorcyclist's highway rights compare with a car driver's, and what restraint applies to both sides?
sec08-card-sec08-F02.teaching_text: Drivers must yield full lane and intersection rights, while riders avoid abusing narrow size to thread traffic.

sec08-card-sec08-F03.question_text: Why must you keep more than four seconds behind a motorcycle, especially approaching intersections?
sec08-card-sec08-F03.teaching_text: Rolling off the throttle or downshifting drops motorcycle speed sharply without ever illuminating a red brake lamp.

sec08-card-sec08-F04.question_text: Why shouldn't you pull out immediately just because an approaching motorcycle's turn signal is blinking?
sec08-card-sec08-F04.teaching_text: Many motorcycle signals do not self-cancel after an earlier lane shift, so wait until the bike visibly slows to turn.

sec08-card-sec08-F05.question_text: Why do smart motorcyclists move left, center, or right within their lane during normal riding?
sec08-card-sec08-F05.teaching_text: Shifting lane tracks helps riders stay visible in mirrors and dodge gravel, oil streaks, or truck wind blasts.

sec08-card-sec08-F06.question_text: How does a motorcycle's slim outline trick your eyes on speed and distance before an intersection turn?
sec08-card-sec08-F06.teaching_text: Small silhouettes deceive human depth perception, tempting left-turning drivers to pull out when the bike is close.

sec08-card-sec08-R01.question_text: Given how a small silhouette distorts speed and range, what safe assumption should guide intersection turns?
sec08-card-sec08-R01.teaching_text: Treating an oncoming motorcycle as closer than your eyes suggest prevents cutting across its path.

sec08-card-sec08-F07.question_text: Behind which everyday cabin and roadside objects can an entire motorcycle disappear from view?
sec08-card-sec08-F07.teaching_text: A narrow bike vanishes behind windshield pillars, passengers, fences, or parked cars unless you double-check blind spots.

sec08-card-sec08-F08.question_text: How does a motorcycle's stopping distance compare with a car's, and what happens on slick pavement?
sec08-card-sec08-F08.teaching_text: Two-wheel balance makes hard braking on wet or sandy pavement tricky, so riders cannot stop on a dime.

sec08-card-sec08-F09.question_text: Why shouldn't you count on a motorcycle swerving clear, especially when a second rider is aboard?
sec08-card-sec08-F09.teaching_text: Extra weight on the back seat slows braking, stiffens steering, and makes quick intersection dodges much harder.

sec08-card-sec08-F10.question_text: How do a motorcycle's small convex mirrors distort your car's reflection, and what gap should you hold?
sec08-card-sec08-F10.teaching_text: Curved mirrors make your bumper look smaller and farther back than reality, so maintain at least four seconds.

sec08-card-sec08-F11.question_text: Why do motorists unintentionally overlook motorcycles, and what visual clue matters after dark?
sec08-card-sec08-F11.teaching_text: Drivers tuned to twin car headlights easily miss a lone lamp blending into background traffic glow at night.

sec08-card-sec08-F12.question_text: How must you change lanes and use speed when passing a motorcycle or being passed by one?
sec08-card-sec08-F12.teaching_text: Sharing a rider's lane or speeding up while being overtaken crowds an unprotected motorcyclist at highway speed.

sec08-card-sec08-R02.question_text: What key rule defines passing a motorcycle compared with returning to your lane ahead of a truck?
sec08-card-sec08-R02.teaching_text: Motorcycles demand a complete lane change beside them, whereas large trucks require seeing the whole cab before merging back.

sec08-card-sec08-F29.question_text: What road rights do animal riders and animal-drawn vehicles hold, and how must an approaching driver react?
sec08-card-sec08-F29.teaching_text: Horses spook fast around rushing metal, so slowing down and stopping when needed protects both animal and handler.

sec08-card-sec08-F30.question_text: What noise ban, lane rule, and following cushion apply around ridden horses, wagons, or herded livestock?
sec08-card-sec08-F30.teaching_text: Horns or revving engines can bolt a horse into traffic, so pass quietly in the full adjacent lane.

sec08-card-sec08-R05.question_text: How does Vermont's rule around horses and livestock compare with handling an aggressive driver?
sec08-card-sec08-R05.teaching_text: Livestock need quiet four-second spacing, while aggressive motorists need calm lane yielding with zero retaliation.

sec08-card-sec08-F31.question_text: What legal penalties can hit a motorist who operates negligently around animals on a Vermont highway?
sec08-card-sec08-F31.teaching_text: Reckless or noisy driving around horses and livestock is a punishable offense carrying fines or imprisonment.

sec08-card-sec08-F23.question_text: What rear emblem identifies tractors and slow farm machinery, and how does spotting it help you?
sec08-card-sec08-F23.teaching_text: Recognizing that fluorescent-and-reflective rear triangle early lets you shed highway speed smoothly instead of panic-braking.

sec08-card-sec08-R04.question_text: Which colors and shape mounted on the back identify slow-moving farm equipment?
sec08-card-sec08-R04.teaching_text: That distinct two-tone rear triangle instantly separates slow agricultural machinery from normal highway traffic.

sec08-card-sec08-F24.question_text: Which three width, visibility, and turning surprises make passing farm equipment tricky?
sec08-card-sec08-F24.teaching_text: Tractors swing wide into unmarked field gaps on either side while swaying wagons block your view of the operator.

sec08-card-sec08-F25.question_text: What road right do agricultural operators hold, and why keep four seconds or more behind them?
sec08-card-sec08-F25.teaching_text: Staying well back past four seconds lets the tractor operator spot you in mirrors and pull aside when safe.

sec08-card-sec08-F26.question_text: How should you handle oncoming wide farm machinery on narrow roads, and when may you pass?
sec08-card-sec08-F26.teaching_text: Impatient passes around wide implements cause collisions when a tractor unexpectedly turns toward a field gate.

sec08-card-sec08-F32.question_text: During which three daily periods do moose and deer roam and feed most actively near posted crossings?
sec08-card-sec08-F32.teaching_text: Low-light feeding hours put deadly thousand-pound wildlife on Vermont highways right when visibility drops.

sec08-card-sec08-F33.question_text: How can headlights make a deer react, how fast can it bolt, and why look for another?
sec08-card-sec08-F33.teaching_text: Blinded deer either freeze or sprint forty miles per hour toward cover, with a second deer often trailing right behind.

sec08-card-sec08-F34.question_text: What two physical traits make hitting a moose far deadlier for car occupants than hitting a deer?
sec08-card-sec08-F34.teaching_text: A car bumper sweeps long moose legs out, dropping over a thousand pounds straight onto the windshield and roof.

sec08-card-sec08-F35.question_text: Why are moose much harder to spot in headlights at dusk than deer?
sec08-card-sec08-F35.teaching_text: Low-beam headlights shine underneath a tall moose's eye height while its dark brown coat blends into night trees.

sec08-card-sec08-R06.question_text: Why do deer eyes glow back in car headlights while a moose's eyes usually do not?
sec08-card-sec08-R06.teaching_text: Relying on glowing eyes alone misses tall, dark-coated moose standing right in your lane after sunset.

sec08-card-sec08-F01.question_text: Why do skateboarders, rollerbladers, kick-scooter riders, and electric-wheelchair users demand extra caution?
sec08-card-sec08-F01.teaching_text: Small wheels move surprisingly fast and pivot sharply into traffic without turn signals or brake lights.

sec08-card-sec08-F27.question_text: Which unlawful driving habits and hostile gestures mark an aggressive driver?
sec08-card-sec08-F27.teaching_text: Unsignaled lane darts, tailgating, speeding, and flashing or yelling break traffic laws and trigger high-speed crashes.

sec08-card-sec08-F28.question_text: What is the smart, safe response when an aggressive driver cuts you off or drives dangerously?
sec08-card-sec08-F28.teaching_text: Moving clear and refusing every challenge lets a reckless driver pass harmlessly instead of escalating into a crash.

sec14-card-sec14-F21.question_text: What coverage must any vehicle you drive carry under Vermont's financial responsibility law, and why?
sec14-card-sec14-F21.teaching_text: Carrying active liability coverage shields your personal savings when injury or property crashes happen.

sec14-card-sec14-F22.question_text: What three minimum dollar amounts are required for Vermont motor-vehicle liability insurance?
sec14-card-sec14-F22.teaching_text: Policies below twenty-five thousand single injury, fifty thousand multi-person, or ten thousand property fail state law.

sec14-card-sec14-R02.question_text: Which loss category matches twenty-five thousand, fifty thousand, and ten thousand dollars in Vermont coverage?
sec14-card-sec14-R02.teaching_text: Test traps scramble whether ten thousand covers property damage while twenty-five and fifty cover injuries.

sec14-card-sec14-F23.question_text: Where must your insurer's proof card stay, and during which two occasions must you present it?
sec14-card-sec14-F23.teaching_text: Arriving at your road exam without a valid insurer card cancels the driving test before it starts.

sec14-card-sec14-F24.question_text: What happens if stopped completely uninsured versus insured without the paper card on hand?
sec14-card-sec14-F24.teaching_text: Active policies get fifteen days to prove coverage, while driving uninsured triggers a fine and two points.

sec14-card-sec14-R03.question_text: How does Vermont's roadside penalty separate an uninsured driver from an insured driver missing the card?
sec14-card-sec14-R03.teaching_text: Forgetting your wallet card gives fifteen days to submit proof instead of immediate points and fines.

sec14-card-sec14-F25.question_text: When does driving uninsured cost your license, and how long must future insurance proof stay filed?
sec14-card-sec14-F25.teaching_text: Even a no-fault crash or major violation while uninsured suspends your license and mandates three-year proof.

sec14-card-sec14-F01.question_text: Who must register road vehicles in Vermont, and what deadline applies after moving from out of state?
sec14-card-sec14-F01.teaching_text: Waiting past sixty days after establishing Vermont residency turns out-of-state plates into an unregistered violation.

sec14-card-sec14-R01.question_text: Compare Vermont's deadlines for new-resident registration, mailing vehicle-trade paperwork, and reporting personal or color updates?
sec14-card-sec14-R01.teaching_text: DMV questions love mixing sixty-day residency, twenty-four-hour trade mailings, and thirty-day record updates.
sec14-card-sec14-R01.must_match_memory_hook: Sixty newcomer, twenty-four trade, thirty change

visual_sync.text_span: Sixty newcomer, twenty-four trade, thirty change

sec14-card-sec14-F02.question_text: Where must valid registration proof stay whenever a vehicle is driven, and who can inspect it?
sec14-card-sec14-F02.teaching_text: Leaving your registration slip at home leaves you unable to satisfy a lawful roadside inspection.

sec14-card-sec14-F03.question_text: How must Vermont plates be fastened and maintained, and from how far must rear lighting make them readable?
sec14-card-sec14-F03.teaching_text: Tinted covers, road grime, or burned-out tag bulbs block plate legibility inside fifty feet.

sec14-card-sec14-F04.question_text: Can you share plates across cars you own, and when may old plates move onto another purchase?
sec14-card-sec14-F04.teaching_text: Bolting plates onto a second car without trading or selling the first vehicle is unlawful.

sec14-card-sec14-F10.question_text: Which three owner or vehicle changes must you report to the Vermont DMV within thirty days?
sec14-card-sec14-F10.teaching_text: Even repainting your car a different color requires notifying the DMV within thirty days.

sec14-card-sec14-F05.question_text: What paperwork details and plate step must a seller complete when selling a vehicle?
sec14-card-sec14-F05.teaching_text: Completing the bill of sale, signing title mileage and buyer info, and pulling plates protects sellers.

sec14-card-sec14-F06.question_text: Which vehicle model years require a buyer-and-seller signed odometer statement upon sale, and where does it appear?
sec14-card-sec14-F06.teaching_text: Skipping dual signatures on the title or Vermont bill of sale stalls registration on newer vehicles.

sec14-card-sec14-F07.question_text: What paperwork, plate step, and Montpelier mailing deadline apply when trading vehicles?
sec14-card-sec14-F07.teaching_text: After swapping bills of sale, signing title, and moving plates, Montpelier paperwork mails within twenty-four hours.

sec14-card-sec14-F08.question_text: Through which three channels can you replace a lost Vermont registration certificate?
sec14-card-sec14-F08.teaching_text: Ordering online, mailing a request, or visiting any DMV branch restores required in-car proof fast.

sec14-card-sec14-F09.question_text: Where can you obtain a Replacement Plate Application if one or both plates go missing?
sec14-card-sec14-F09.teaching_text: Local police stations stock replacement plate forms alongside DMV offices and the state website.

sec14-card-sec14-F11.question_text: How is Vermont's six-percent purchase and use tax calculated on a bought, non-leased vehicle?
sec14-card-sec14-F11.teaching_text: Understating a private sale price will not cut tax when fair market value sits higher.

sec14-card-sec14-R04.question_text: How does Vermont's six-percent tax base differ between buying a vehicle outright and leasing one?
sec14-card-sec14-R04.teaching_text: Purchases tax the higher of price or market value while leases subtract lease-end value first.

sec14-card-sec14-F12.question_text: Under what two conditions is a newcomer's previously owned out-of-state vehicle exempt from Vermont purchase tax?
sec14-card-sec14-F12.teaching_text: Paying lower tax elsewhere without three years registered in a taxing jurisdiction leaves the difference owed.

sec14-card-sec14-F13.question_text: Which documents verify lease tax on a Vermont-dealer lease, and what happens if none accompany registration?
sec14-card-sec14-F13.teaching_text: Omitting the computation form, lease contract, or dealer worksheet triggers six percent on full acquisition cost.

sec14-card-sec14-F14.question_text: How is taxable cost figured on a documented lease, and does a buyout option change it?
sec14-card-sec14-F14.teaching_text: Subtracting stated lease-end value from acquisition cost sets the six-percent base whether buyout exists or not.

sec14-card-sec14-F15.question_text: Which motorcycles and trailers are exempt from Vermont's general motor-vehicle title requirement?
sec14-card-sec14-F15.teaching_text: Motorcycles below three hundred cubic centimeters and trailers fifteen hundred pounds or lighter skip titling.

sec14-card-sec14-F16.question_text: Which special document is mandatory to register a brand-new vehicle alongside standard Vermont registration papers?
sec14-card-sec14-F16.teaching_text: Brand-new vehicles cannot register without an origin certificate, while used registrations require the signed prior title.

sec14-card-sec14-F17.question_text: What makes up a modern vehicle identification number, and when did seventeen characters become standard?
sec14-card-sec14-F17.teaching_text: Pre-nineteen-eighty-one vehicles carried eleven to seventeen characters before the standardized seventeen-character alphanumeric format began.

sec14-card-sec14-R06.question_text: All post-nineteen-eighty-one cars carry seventeen-character codes, so which three registration categories require physical verification?
sec14-card-sec14-R06.teaching_text: Standard domestic clean-title cars skip physical inspection while salvage, bonded, and foreign imports require verification.

sec14-card-sec14-F18.question_text: Which three vehicle types need identification-number verification, and who in Vermont may perform it?
sec14-card-sec14-F18.teaching_text: Canadian or foreign imports, bonded titles, and salvage cars require Vermont police or designated DMV verification.

sec14-card-sec14-F19.question_text: How is a Vermont title branded after registering a salvage vehicle, and what check comes first?
sec14-card-sec14-F19.teaching_text: Vermont police or a DMV employee must verify the identification number on your application before branding.

sec14-card-sec14-F20.question_text: What does a car loan place on your vehicle, and who keeps the title until payoff?
sec14-card-sec14-F20.teaching_text: Listing the lender on your registration sends the physical title straight to the lien holder until payoff.

sec14-card-sec14-F26.question_text: How often must Vermont vehicles pass inspection, and how soon after new registration without a valid sticker?
sec14-card-sec14-F26.teaching_text: Neglecting mechanical upkeep risks crash liability on top of missing your fifteen-day new-car deadline.

sec14-card-sec14-R05.question_text: How does Vermont's fifteen-day inspection rule pair with ongoing sticker renewals?
sec14-card-sec14-R05.teaching_text: Newly registered cars without current stickers get fifteen days first and renew every twelve months afterward.

sec14-card-sec14-F27.question_text: How much fuel economy can cruising fifty-five or sixty instead of sixty-five on the interstate save?
sec14-card-sec14-F27.teaching_text: Easing back five to ten miles per hour on highways cuts wind drag for major mileage gains.

sec14-card-sec14-F28.question_text: How do jackrabbit starts, lane weaving, and hard braking hurt both fuel use and vehicle parts?
sec14-card-sec14-F28.teaching_text: Keeping generous following space lets you anticipate slowdowns gradually instead of burning fuel and brake pads.

sec14-card-sec14-F29.question_text: How long should stationary winter warm-ups and in-town idling stay to protect lungs, engines, and fuel?
sec14-card-sec14-F29.teaching_text: Scraping snow before starting and shutting off past ten seconds in town saves fuel over idling.

sec14-card-sec14-F30.question_text: What does Vermont's unattended motor-vehicle law require whenever you step away in public?
sec14-card-sec14-F30.teaching_text: Leaving an engine running unattended in public breaks state law even during freezing winter errands.

sec14-card-sec14-F31.question_text: Where is recommended tire pressure listed, and how much fuel can proper inflation save?
sec14-card-sec14-F31.teaching_text: Underinflated tires boost rolling drag and wear tread early compared with door-jamb and manual specs.

sec14-card-sec14-F32.question_text: Which upkeep items and cargo habits prevent making your engine burn extra fuel?
sec14-card-sec14-F32.teaching_text: Out-of-alignment wheels, clogged air filters, trunk clutter, and roof cargo force harder engine work.

sec14-card-sec14-F33.question_text: How much fuel can trimming air-conditioner use above eighty degrees save, and what habits help?
sec14-card-sec14-F33.teaching_text: Parking in shade and using fresh-air vents trims heavy compressor load on eighty-plus-degree days.

sec14-card-sec14-F34.question_text: Above what speed should windows stay closed to prevent drag, and what trip habits cut fuel?
sec14-card-sec14-F34.teaching_text: Open windows at fifty miles per hour or faster create wind drag while carpooling trims miles.

sec06-card-sec06-F01.question_text: What does a railroad crossbuck sign mark, and what three actions should you take before crossing?
sec06-card-sec06-F01.teaching_text: Every rail crossing carries a crossbuck right at the tracks, demanding reduced speed plus visual and audio checks.

sec06-card-sec06-F02.question_text: What does the small plaque below a crossbuck show, and what hidden danger comes with multiple tracks?
sec06-card-sec06-F02.teaching_text: Pulling out right behind one caboose can put you straight into a second locomotive approaching from the opposite direction.

sec06-card-sec06-F03.question_text: Where will you see a triangle sign with its three points cut off, and what does it mean?
sec06-card-sec06-F03.teaching_text: Spotting that clipped-point triangle on farm machinery warns you early that closing speed is much faster than normal.

sec06-card-sec06-F04.question_text: What shape and colors identify standard warning signs, and what driver action do they call for?
sec06-card-sec06-F04.teaching_text: Sharp curves, road dips, and tricky intersections pose constant hazards that require dropping speed before you reach them.

sec06-card-sec06-R01.question_text: How do you tell a roadside warning sign apart from a slow-moving farm emblem by shape?
sec06-card-sec06-R01.teaching_text: Roadside hazards stand on four-pointed yellow or green diamonds, whereas slow farm rigs wear clipped-corner triangles.

sec06-card-sec06-F05.question_text: What extra details can accompany a warning sign, and what does a downward arrow under a pedestrian or school sign mark?
sec06-card-sec06-F05.teaching_text: While advance signs warn ahead, a downward-pointing plaque pinpoints the exact spot where walkers step into your lane.

sec06-card-sec06-F06.question_text: What shape and background color mark regulatory signs, and what kind of message do they give?
sec06-card-sec06-F06.teaching_text: Speed limits, turn rules, and passing bans appear on white rectangles because they state enforceable commands, not suggestions.

sec06-card-sec06-R02.question_text: When snow or dirt hides a sign's lettering, how does shape separate regulatory rules from hazard warnings?
sec06-card-sec06-R02.teaching_text: Even with ice crusting the face, a vertical rectangle signals a legal command while a diamond warns of danger.

sec06-card-sec06-F23.question_text: Which color and two shapes identify work-zone signs, and what hazards do they announce?
sec06-card-sec06-F23.teaching_text: Bright orange alerts you early to closed lanes, detours, rough pavement, or flaggers ahead.

sec06-card-sec06-R06.question_text: Alongside orange diamond or rectangular work signs, what legal status does a work-zone flagger hold?
sec06-card-sec06-R06.teaching_text: Ignoring a crew flagger's paddle or hand direction carries the same legal violation as running an official traffic control.

sec06-card-sec06-F07.question_text: What four jobs do highway pavement markings perform, and what color are center lines on major highways?
sec06-card-sec06-F07.teaching_text: Painted stripes keep cars positioned, guide turns, regulate passing, and separate opposing traffic with yellow center markings.

sec06-card-sec06-F08.question_text: On an undivided multilane road, what separates opposing directions versus lanes moving the same way?
sec06-card-sec06-F08.teaching_text: Crossing double solid center stripes puts you into head-on traffic, while broken white dashes divide parallel lanes.

sec06-card-sec06-R04.question_text: How do double solid yellow lines contrast with broken white lines on an undivided multilane highway?
sec06-card-sec06-R04.teaching_text: One glance at paint color tells you whether adjacent cars are coming straight at you or rolling your way.

sec06-card-sec06-F09.question_text: How do single solid, double solid, and paired broken-and-solid center lines control passing?
sec06-card-sec06-F09.teaching_text: Solid stripes on your side mean sight distance is unsafe, whereas a broken stripe on your side allows clear passes.

sec06-card-sec06-R03.question_text: When one center stripe is solid and the other is broken, which stripe governs your lane?
sec06-card-sec06-R03.teaching_text: A broken stripe on the far side helps oncoming cars only; a solid stripe beside your left tire forbids passing.

sec06-card-sec06-F27.question_text: In a work zone with temporary markers, which color belongs on your left, and what if it is not?
sec06-card-sec06-F27.teaching_text: Shifted construction lanes confuse drivers fast, and seeing yellow temporary markers on your right means wrong-way travel.

sec06-card-sec06-F10.question_text: How must you enter and use a continuous two-way left-turn lane, and what is it never used for?
sec06-card-sec06-F10.teaching_text: Because opposing traffic shares that center space, cruising or passing inside it sets up head-on collisions.

sec06-card-sec06-F11.question_text: What does a painted row of white triangles pointing toward approaching vehicles mark at an intersection?
sec06-card-sec06-F11.teaching_text: Stopping behind those shark-tooth triangles keeps your bumper clear of crosswalk walkers and cross-street traffic.

sec06-card-sec06-F12.question_text: When turning onto a multilane road, which lane must a right-turning driver and a left-turning driver each enter first?
sec06-card-sec06-F12.teaching_text: Swinging wide across multiple lanes mid-turn sideswipes drivers legally turning from the opposite approach.

sec06-card-sec06-F13.question_text: When are multiple lanes allowed to turn together, and how must each driver track through the turn?
sec06-card-sec06-F13.teaching_text: Drifting out of your curved guide lane mid-intersection clips the car turning right beside you.

sec06-card-sec06-F14.question_text: Why must you finish a turn completely before changing lanes?
sec06-card-sec06-F14.teaching_text: Switching lanes inside an intersection is illegal and catches nearby turning traffic completely off guard.

sec06-card-sec06-R05.question_text: What separates a legal post-turn lane change from an illegal turn maneuver?
sec06-card-sec06-R05.teaching_text: Completing the turn into your assigned lane first makes the next signaled lane shift predictable and legal.

sec06-card-sec06-F15.question_text: If you realize too late that you are in a straight-arrow lane when you wanted to turn, what should you do?
sec06-card-sec06-F15.teaching_text: Turning from a straight-only lane breaks the law and causes crashes, whereas looping the block costs seconds.

sec06-card-sec06-F16.question_text: What activities count as a highway work zone, including slow-moving mobile operations?
sec06-card-sec06-F16.teaching_text: Paint-striping trucks, mowers, and snowplows create moving work zones that deserve the same caution as coned sites.

sec06-card-sec06-F17.question_text: Where do many work-zone collisions actually occur, and what crash type is most common?
sec06-card-sec06-F17.teaching_text: Speeding and tailgating into slowdowns hidden over hills or curves cause rear-end pileups before the cones even start.

sec06-card-sec06-F18.question_text: Do work-zone speed and safety rules stop overnight, and how should you adjust speed in bad weather?
sec06-card-sec06-F18.teaching_text: Narrow lanes, drop-offs, and night crews remain hazardous after dark, so posted work limits apply twenty-four hours a day.

sec06-card-sec06-F19.question_text: What focus and lane discipline does the Vermont manual expect from drivers inside a work zone?
sec06-card-sec06-F19.teaching_text: Watching for walkers and cyclists while skipping tailgating or abrupt lane hops keeps tight construction chutes safe.

sec06-card-sec06-F20.question_text: What following gap and merging habits protect crews and traffic through a work zone?
sec06-card-sec06-F20.teaching_text: Merging promptly, giving workers wide berth, and holding a four-second cushion absorb sudden construction stops.

sec06-card-sec06-F21.question_text: On dry pavement, how many feet does a passenger car need to stop from sixty miles per hour versus thirty?
sec06-card-sec06-F21.teaching_text: Doubling your speed from thirty to sixty more than triples dry stopping distance from seventy-five to two hundred forty feet.

sec06-card-sec06-F22.question_text: What happens to the fine penalty if you are caught speeding in a Vermont work zone?
sec06-card-sec06-F22.teaching_text: Vermont doubles speeding fines in roadwork zones to deter high-speed crashes around exposed crews.

sec06-card-sec06-F24.question_text: Why does work-zone traffic often stop completely, and what tools and authority do flaggers use?
sec06-card-sec06-F24.teaching_text: Moving heavy machinery or alternating one shared lane requires flaggers whose paddles and flags carry binding legal authority.

sec06-card-sec06-F25.question_text: What role do cones, drums, and barricades serve as channeling devices in a work zone?
sec06-card-sec06-F25.teaching_text: Orange cones, barrels, and barricades block off open trenches and crews while steering traffic along a safe path.

sec06-card-sec06-F26.question_text: Besides directional merge arrows, what does caution mode look like on a flashing work-zone panel, and what does it mean?
sec06-card-sec06-F26.teaching_text: A horizontal blinking bar or four flashing corners means no lane shift is required, yet you must slow down.

sec09-card-sec09-F21.question_text: What driver mistake causes most skids on slick surfaces, and which convenience feature must stay off?
sec09-card-sec09-F21.teaching_text: Failing to slow ahead of snow, ice, rain, gravel, or wet leaves breaks traction, and cruise control worsens wheelspin.

sec09-card-sec09-F22.question_text: How does skid warning differ between rear-wheel and front-wheel drive, and what snow trap catches front-wheel drivers?
sec09-card-sec09-F22.teaching_text: Front-wheel pull feels confident in snow yet breaks loose abruptly without warning if it tempts you into higher speed.

sec09-card-sec09-F23.question_text: With standard non-ABS brakes, how should you shed speed on a slippery road without locking the wheels?
sec09-card-sec09-F23.teaching_text: Coasting off the throttle first and squeezing gently keeps tires rolling; if wheels start locking, ease pressure slightly.

sec09-card-sec09-R01.question_text: On slick pavement, how does proper pedal work differ between ordinary brakes and anti-lock brakes?
sec09-card-sec09-R01.teaching_text: Standard brakes require easing off if wheels lock, whereas anti-lock computers pulse automatically only while you hold firm.

sec09-card-sec09-R02.question_text: How does brake use change once you switch from preventing a skid to recovering from an active skid?
sec09-card-sec09-R02.teaching_text: Gentle braking helps before traction breaks, whereas touching the brake mid-skid locks sideways tires and ruins steering recovery.

sec09-card-sec09-F24.question_text: How should you press the brake pedal in an anti-lock-equipped car, and what old habit must you avoid?
sec09-card-sec09-F24.teaching_text: Pumping an anti-lock pedal defeats the rapid computer modulation designed to prevent wheel lockup.

sec09-card-sec09-F25.question_text: Whether driving front- or rear-wheel drive, what exact steps bring a skidding vehicle back under control?
sec09-card-sec09-F25.teaching_text: Keeping off the brake and steering smoothly toward your intended lane while counter-correcting left and right restores grip.

sec09-card-sec09-F26.question_text: Do stability systems or all-wheel drive help you grip glare ice, and where should you test winter handling?
sec09-card-sec09-F26.teaching_text: All-wheel drive pulls through snow yet slides on ice like anything else, so practice gently in an empty lot.

sec09-card-sec09-F27.question_text: What crucial maneuver do anti-lock brakes allow, and what normal pedal sensations happen when they activate?
sec09-card-sec09-F27.teaching_text: Startled drivers lift off when the pedal chatters and vibrates, losing the ability to brake hard while steering clear.

sec09-card-sec09-F28.question_text: What foot mistake turns anti-lock protection off mid-stop, and how do you confirm your car has ABS?
sec09-card-sec09-F28.teaching_text: Check your owner's manual and watch for the brief startup dash bulb, then keep steady foot pressure in emergencies.

sec09-card-sec09-R03.question_text: How do you interpret an anti-lock dash light that blinks briefly at startup versus one staying lit on the road?
sec09-card-sec09-R03.teaching_text: A brief bulb check confirms working sensors, while a steady dash light warns that anti-lock assist is offline.

sec09-card-sec09-F29.question_text: If your anti-lock brake warning light stays illuminated while driving, do you still have working brakes?
sec09-card-sec09-F29.teaching_text: You lose automatic anti-lock pulsing until serviced, though ordinary hydraulic brakes still stop the car.

sec09-card-sec09-F08.question_text: Which headlight beam belongs in fog or heavy snow, and at what visibility distance does Vermont require headlights?
sec09-card-sec09-F08.teaching_text: High beams bounce blinding glare off fog droplets, and Vermont law requires headlights whenever sight drops under five hundred feet.

sec09-card-sec09-F30.question_text: By how much do daytime low-beam headlights cut head-on crash risk, and what trap comes with daytime running lights?
sec09-card-sec09-F30.teaching_text: Daytime low beams drop head-on risk over twenty percent, whereas automatic running lights leave taillights dark.

sec09-card-sec09-F31.question_text: When weather limits sight, what lights are required, and when are parking lights legal to use?
sec09-card-sec09-F31.teaching_text: Cruising in rain, snow, or fog on dim parking bulbs is unlawful because parking lights belong strictly on parked cars.

sec09-card-sec09-F32.question_text: During which exact night hours does Vermont law require headlights, and why switch them on manually?
sec09-card-sec09-F32.teaching_text: Dashboard glow and daytime running lamps trick drivers into driving after dark without full headlights or taillights.

sec09-card-sec09-R04.question_text: What two independent legal triggers, one by clock and one by sight distance, require headlights in Vermont?
sec09-card-sec09-R04.teaching_text: Even at noon, heavy fog or snow cutting visibility inside five hundred feet triggers the exact same headlight mandate.

sec09-card-sec09-F33.question_text: What sight cushion do you always need ahead, and at what night speed are you already overdriving low beams?
sec09-card-sec09-F33.teaching_text: At forty miles per hour after dark on low beams, your stopping distance already stretches past the lit pavement.

sec09-card-sec09-F34.question_text: Where do high beams belong at night, and which four situations require switching to low beams?
sec09-card-sec09-F34.teaching_text: Open rural roads suit high beams at moderated speed, while oncoming cars, following, streetlights, and fog demand low beams.

sec09-card-sec09-R05.question_text: How do high beams, low beams, and daytime running lights divide up open country, traffic or fog, and full headlights?
sec09-card-sec09-R05.teaching_text: Never substitute daytime running lamps when conditions require real low beams or open-country high beams.

sec09-card-sec09-F35.question_text: When should you dim high beams for others, and where should you aim your eyes if oncoming lights blind you?
sec09-card-sec09-F35.teaching_text: Glancing ahead along the right road edge preserves night vision and lane tracking until glaring headlights pass.

sec09-card-sec09-F01.question_text: How deadly are flash floods nationwide for motorists, and what is the smartest call when severe weather is forecast?
sec09-card-sec09-F01.teaching_text: Nearly half of all flash-flood fatalities happen in vehicles, making canceling nonessential trips the safest move.

sec09-card-sec09-F02.question_text: What speed, cruise-control, and following-gap adjustments apply if a storm hits while you are driving?
sec09-card-sec09-F02.teaching_text: Dropping speed, shutting off cruise control, and opening past four seconds gives wet tires vital stopping margin.

sec09-card-sec09-F03.question_text: Why must you obey detour signs and never drive past road-closed signs or around flood barricades?
sec09-card-sec09-F03.teaching_text: Calm-looking water behind a barricade can conceal a collapsed culvert or missing bridge deck.

sec09-card-sec09-F04.question_text: What three dangers make driving across water-covered pavement a trap?
sec09-card-sec09-F04.teaching_text: Flooded asphalt hides deep washouts and drowns engines fast, trapping occupants inside rising current.

sec09-card-sec09-F05.question_text: What must you do immediately if your car stalls in floodwater, and how shallow can dangerous moving water be?
sec09-card-sec09-F05.teaching_text: Staying to push or restart a flooded car kills motorists, and just four inches of current impairs footing.

sec09-card-sec09-F06.question_text: Which vehicles feel strong crosswinds worst, and how must you treat storm-downed trees and utility wires?
sec09-card-sec09-F06.teaching_text: High-profile trucks and trailers catch gusts hardest, and downed utility lines can energize wet pavement fatally.

sec09-card-sec09-F07.question_text: Which official alerts should every driver check before heading out in questionable weather?
sec09-card-sec09-F07.teaching_text: Checking flash-flood alerts and travel advisories before leaving home keeps you out of impassable storm corridors.

sec09-card-sec09-F09.question_text: Which vehicle systems and two cold-weather fluids must be ready before Vermont winter arrives?
sec09-card-sec09-F09.teaching_text: Tight exhaust prevents carbon monoxide leaks while strong brakes, wipers, defroster, antifreeze, and winter washer fluid maintain control.

sec09-card-sec09-F10.question_text: How many wheels need snow tires before the first snowfall, and what tire-mixing mistake must you avoid?
sec09-card-sec09-F10.teaching_text: Mounting snow tires on only two wheels or mixing mismatched tire types creates dangerous spinouts in corners.

sec09-card-sec09-F12.question_text: If you must drive during a winter storm, how thoroughly must you clear the car, wipers, and glass?
sec09-card-sec09-F12.teaching_text: Peephole scraping leaves blind spots and roof snow slides onto windshields or trailing cars under braking.

sec09-card-sec09-F13.question_text: Which three elevated road structures freeze before regular pavement when sleet or freezing rain starts?
sec09-card-sec09-F13.teaching_text: Cold air circulates both above and underneath elevated decks, glazing invisible black ice while main roads look wet.

sec09-card-sec09-F14.question_text: How much following gap do winter roads demand, and why can't four-wheel drive shorten your braking?
sec09-card-sec09-F14.teaching_text: All four brakes already work on every car, so four-wheel drive adds zero stopping or cornering grip on ice.

sec09-card-sec09-R06.question_text: Why must four-wheel and all-wheel-drive drivers still stretch winter following distances past four seconds?
sec09-card-sec09-R06.teaching_text: Getting moving easily in deep snow lulls drivers into forgetting that ice stops every drivetrain equally poorly.

sec09-card-sec09-F16.question_text: What survival gear belongs in a Vermont winter car kit, and what minimum fuel reading should you keep?
sec09-card-sec09-F16.teaching_text: Keeping at least half a tank prevents fuel-line freeze and powers heat if a blizzard strands you.

sec09-card-sec09-F11.question_text: When do many states permit metal-studded tires, and what tire maintenance rule applies year-round?
sec09-card-sec09-F11.teaching_text: Cold air drops tire pressure fast, and many states restrict metal studs strictly to winter months.

sec09-card-sec09-F15.question_text: What three traits make snowplows tricky to share the road with, and how should winter trips be planned?
sec09-card-sec09-F15.teaching_text: Wide plows disappear inside swirling snow plumes, and daytime main-road travel with someone knowing your schedule boosts safety.

sec09-card-sec09-F17.question_text: If a blizzard strands you, how should you mark the car, and why stay inside instead of walking?
sec09-card-sec09-F17.teaching_text: Blowing whiteouts distort distance fatally, whereas rescuers spot a flagged vehicle with hazard flashers along the road.

sec09-card-sec09-F18.question_text: When stranded in snow, how long should you run the heater each hour, and what two steps stop carbon monoxide?
sec09-card-sec09-F18.teaching_text: Drifting snow plugging the exhaust pipe fills a sealed cabin with odorless, lethal carbon monoxide in minutes.

sec09-card-sec09-F19.question_text: How should stranded occupants stay warm and alert inside the cabin, and which drink must they never touch?
sec09-card-sec09-F19.teaching_text: Alcohol speeds body-heat loss and drowsiness, whereas light movement, floor-mat insulation, and sleep shifts keep everyone alive.

sec09-card-sec09-F20.question_text: How should a stranded driver ration battery power, stay visible at night, and signal search aircraft in open snow?
sec09-card-sec09-F20.teaching_text: Using the dome lamp at night helps ground crews, while rock-lined HELP or SOS letters guide search planes.

sec11-card-sec11-F02.question_text: What ranks as the number-one cause of fatal crashes, and how often does a drunk-driving death occur on average?
sec11-card-sec11-F02.teaching_text: Drinking drivers top fatal crash statistics nationwide, claiming another life roughly every forty minutes.

sec11-card-sec11-F03.question_text: Why does Vermont law ban driving under the influence of alcohol or other drugs?
sec11-card-sec11-F03.teaching_text: Alcohol and drugs strip personal and vehicle control, risking both the driver and everyone nearby.

sec11-card-sec11-F04.question_text: At what blood alcohol concentration does Vermont law treat any driver as impaired, and does impairment start lower?
sec11-card-sec11-F04.teaching_text: Even well below point zero eight, a single drink already clouds driving judgment.

sec11-card-sec11-R01.question_text: How does Vermont's point zero eight BAC threshold compare with the point zero two threshold?
sec11-card-sec11-R01.teaching_text: Point zero eight marks general legal impairment, while point zero two already suspends drivers under twenty-one.

sec11-card-sec11-F05.question_text: Which three consequences hit a driver under twenty-one caught at point zero two BAC or higher?
sec11-card-sec11-F05.teaching_text: Underage drinking drivers lose their license and pay out of pocket for mandatory alcohol education.

sec11-card-sec11-F11.question_text: Which six legal and financial consequences follow a DUI or drugged-driving conviction?
sec11-card-sec11-F11.teaching_text: Beyond losing your license and risking jail, legal bills, mandatory classes, and insurance spikes linger years.
sec11-card-sec11-F11.must_match_memory_hook: Suspension, fine, lawyer, class, jail, insurance

sec11-card-sec11-F12.question_text: What does holding a Vermont license imply when police suspect impairment, and what does refusing cost?
sec11-card-sec11-F12.teaching_text: Refusing an officer's alcohol or drug test forfeits your license for at least six months.

sec11-card-sec11-R02.question_text: Does refusing an implied-consent test depend on being convicted of DUI in criminal court?
sec11-card-sec11-R02.teaching_text: Refusal triggers at least six months of license loss all on its own, separate from DUI penalties.

sec11-card-sec11-F13.question_text: How can Vermont's administrative suspension process take a license before any criminal DUI trial finishes?
sec11-card-sec11-F13.teaching_text: Civil administrative action removes impaired drivers' licenses fast without waiting months for criminal court.

sec11-card-sec11-R03.question_text: How do the consequences of civil administrative suspension differ from a criminal DUI conviction?
sec11-card-sec11-R03.teaching_text: Civil suspension pulls your license early, while criminal conviction brings fines, classes, jail, and rate hikes.

sec11-card-sec11-F06.question_text: What class of drug is alcohol, and how does it affect human thinking?
sec11-card-sec11-F06.teaching_text: Instead of giving a mental lift, alcohol slows brain processing and warps judgment.

sec11-card-sec11-F07.question_text: Which four mental and visual abilities degrade together after drinking alcohol?
sec11-card-sec11-F07.teaching_text: Drivers stop sensing danger, lose visual sharpness, drift mentally, and miss what they are doing.

sec11-card-sec11-F08.question_text: How does alcohol trick your sense of speed and affect moving your foot to the brake?
sec11-card-sec11-F08.teaching_text: Dulled senses cause unintentional speeding right as delayed foot reaction stretches emergency stops.

sec11-card-sec11-F09.question_text: What is the only cure for alcohol impairment, and how fast does the body process drinks?
sec11-card-sec11-F09.teaching_text: Coffee, cold showers, and jogging fail completely because the liver needs at least an hour per drink.

sec11-card-sec11-R04.question_text: Can hot coffee, cold showers, or exercise lower your blood alcohol concentration?
sec11-card-sec11-R04.teaching_text: Caffeine or cold water only creates a wide-awake impaired driver with unchanged blood alcohol.

sec11-card-sec11-F16.question_text: Why do coffee, showers, and exercise leave a drinker unsafe to drive?
sec11-card-sec11-F16.teaching_text: None of such home remedies accelerate alcohol elimination below one minimum hour per drink.

sec11-card-sec11-F17.question_text: What do roadside signs sponsored by the Vermont Emergency Nurses Association mark?
sec11-card-sec11-F17.teaching_text: Each roadside marker honors a life lost at an exact location because of a drunk driver.

sec11-card-sec11-F18.question_text: Which free, confidential Vermont service connects people worried about drinking or drug use with support?
sec11-card-sec11-F18.teaching_text: Vermont Helplink provides free, private alcohol and drug referrals through the Department of Health.

sec11-card-sec11-F19.question_text: What crash pattern often follows falling asleep driving, and how can a drowsy driver look to others?
sec11-card-sec11-F19.teaching_text: Unchecked lane drift into oncoming cars or trees makes sleepy drivers weave just like drunk motorists.

sec11-card-sec11-F20.question_text: Which five warning signs tell you drowsiness is taking over your driving?
sec11-card-sec11-F20.teaching_text: Missing road signs, forgetting miles, yawning, or wandering lanes means stop immediately.
sec11-card-sec11-F20.must_match_memory_hook: Heavy eyes, yawning, amnesia, drifting, signs

visual_sync.text_span: Heavy eyes, yawning, amnesia, drifting, signs

sec11-card-sec11-F21.question_text: Which four driver groups face elevated drowsy-driving risk?
sec11-card-sec11-F21.teaching_text: Short-slept young drivers, night-shift workers, and people with undiagnosed sleep disorders nod off unexpectedly.

sec11-card-sec11-F22.question_text: What does reaching for the window switch or radio knob prove when you feel sleepy?
sec11-card-sec11-F22.teaching_text: Fresh air and loud music fail to stop sleep, so hunting wake-up tricks means pull over now.

sec11-card-sec11-R05.question_text: Even though a drowsy driver weaves like a drunk driver, what is the true remedy for drowsiness?
sec11-card-sec11-R05.teaching_text: Only proper sleep restores brain alertness when exhaustion mimics drunk-driving lane drift.

sec11-card-sec11-F01.question_text: Besides alcohol, which other everyday substances and physical state seriously impair driving?
sec11-card-sec11-F01.teaching_text: Pharmacy allergy pills, prescriptions, and lack of sleep degrade driving safety alongside alcohol.

sec11-card-sec11-F10.question_text: How dangerous can narcotics, prescription drugs, or over-the-counter medicines be behind the wheel, and what clears them?
sec11-card-sec11-F10.teaching_text: Drug-induced drowsiness and foggy thinking rival or exceed alcohol danger until time clears your system.

sec11-card-sec11-F14.question_text: What two safe-ride options should you arrange before drinking starts?
sec11-card-sec11-F14.teaching_text: Lining up a drug-and-alcohol-free driver or calling a parent beforehand guarantees everyone gets home.

sec11-card-sec11-F15.question_text: Which three additional choices keep someone who has been drinking off the road?
sec11-card-sec11-F15.teaching_text: Giving keys early to a sober friend or staying put removes impaired temptation completely.
